AI.tldr: A rest-state formulation for reconstructing articulated objects from a single closed configuration, using explicit meshes for cross-model fusion and video diffusion for joint parameter estimation without observable motion.
AI.motivation: Existing articulated object reconstruction methods require explicitly observable motion from multiple articulation states, limiting their applicability to settings where such motion data is unavailable.
AI.method: Adopts an explicit mesh as an intermediate representation for cross-model verification and fusion of vision-language and segmentation model outputs; uses a video diffusion model to synthesize articulation hypotheses and validates them via geometric consistency to estimate joint parameters without observed motion.
AI.result: Achieves accurate part decomposition and physically plausible articulation, performing competitively with motion-observing reconstruction-based, generation-based, and modular pretrained-model baselines.
AI.conclusion: The rest-state formulation effectively compensates for the absence of motion cues using geometry, semantics, and motion priors, demonstrating that articulated objects can be reconstructed from a single closed configuration.

title: EgoGVAE: Ego-body Mesh Reconstruction via Guided Variational Autoencoder
summary: We address the problem of recovering the full-body mesh from only the head pose. This task has become essential for various applications based on head-mounted devices or smart glasses. The challenge of this task lies in estimating the pose information of unobserved body parts based solely on a single joint (i.e., head) trajectory. Several studies have begun to adopt head-conditioned generative models, however, such previous methods are costly and time-consuming due to the diffusion-based iterative process. As an alternative, we propose a simple yet novel method that leverages the latent space of the guidance network, which is designed as a variational autoencoder taking full-body poses as inputs. By enforcing latent distributions of this guidance network and our head-to-motion network to be similar, latent features sampled from the 'guided' distribution, i.e., distribution learned in our head-to-motion network, can be reliably decoded for natural representations of full-body poses even only with the head pose. One important advantage of the proposed method is that one-step sampling scheme achieves remarkably fast inference (more than 50 times faster) compared to diffusion-based approaches. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that the proposed method efficiently improves the performance of ego-body mesh reconstruction.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a fast method for recovering full-body mesh from only head pose by leveraging the latent space of a guidance network (VAE trained on full-body poses). A head-to-motion network is trained to match the latent distribution of the guidance network, enabling one-step sampling that is over 50x faster than diffusion-based approaches while achieving competitive performance on ego-body mesh reconstruction benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Full-body mesh reconstruction from head pose is essential for head-mounted device and smart glasses applications. Existing head-conditioned generative models rely on diffusion-based iterative processes, which are costly and time-consuming.
AI.method: The method uses a guidance network (VAE taking full-body poses as input) and a head-to-motion network. By enforcing the latent distributions of both networks to be similar, latent features sampled from the guided distribution can be reliably decoded into natural full-body poses using only head pose input. This enables one-step sampling instead of iterative diffusion.
AI.result: The one-step sampling scheme achieves remarkably fast inference (more than 50 times faster) compared to diffusion-based approaches, while efficiently improving ego-body mesh reconstruction performance on benchmark datasets.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method provides an efficient alternative to diffusion-based head-conditioned full-body pose estimation, achieving both speed and quality improvements through latent space alignment between the guidance and head-to-motion networks.

title: DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmedical 2026: Architectural Diversity for Concept Detection and Foundation-Model Scaling for Caption Prediction in Medical Image Analysis
summary: We describe the DS@GT submissions to the ImageCLEFmedical Caption 2026 challenge, which continues a long-running benchmark on the ROCOv2 dataset with two tracks: Concept Detection (Task 1), assigning UMLS Concept Unique Identifiers (CUIs) to radiology images, and Caption Prediction (Task 2), generating natural-language captions. For Task 1, our primary submission was a three-way late-fusion ensemble of ConvNeXt-V2, BiomedCLIP ViT-B/16, and DenseNet-169 with a regularized ''Honest Threshold Tuning'' procedure designed to avoid validation overfitting on rare concepts; this submission ranked first on the official submission with a primary $F_1$ of $0.5790$ and a secondary $F_1$ of $0.9657$. In parallel, we submitted a training-free KNN retrieval pipeline over frozen BiomedCLIP embeddings, which reached a primary $F_1$ of $0.5780$ and a secondary $F_1$ of $0.9599$-essentially matching the fine-tuned ensemble on the primary track at a fraction of the cost. For Task 2, our submissions included a fine-tuned Gemma-3 27B model (overall $0.3571$, ranking third in the official submission), a fully fine-tuned BLIP pipeline with custom Vizwins merging ($0.3564$), and a zero-shot MedGemma-4B run with a PubMed-style prompt ($0.3186$), spanning a wide range of model scales and training costs. Code: https://github.com/dsgt-arc/imageclef-caption-2026.

AI.tldr: The DS@GT submissions to the ImageCLEFmedical Caption 2026 challenge, featuring a first-place ensemble (ConvNeXt-V2, BiomedCLIP, DenseNet-169) for Concept Detection with an Honest Threshold Tuning procedure, and multiple captioning approaches (Gemma-3 27B, BLIP, MedGemma-4B) for Caption Prediction, with code publicly released.
AI.motivation: To address the ImageCLEFmedical Caption 2026 benchmark on the ROCOv2 dataset, targeting both concept detection (assigning UMLS CUIs to radiology images) and caption generation, while exploring cost-effective alternatives to expensive fine-tuning.
AI.method: For Task 1: three-way late-fusion ensemble of ConvNeXt-V2, BiomedCLIP ViT-B/16, and DenseNet-169 with regularized "Honest Threshold Tuning" to avoid validation overfitting on rare concepts; also a training-free KNN retrieval over frozen BiomedCLIP embeddings. For Task 2: fine-tuned Gemma-3 27B, fully fine-tuned BLIP pipeline with custom Vizwins merging, and zero-shot MedGemma-4B with PubMed-style prompting.
AI.result: Task 1 ensemble ranked first (primary F1 0.5790, secondary F1 0.9657); KNN retrieval nearly matched it (primary F1 0.5780, secondary F1 0.9599). Task 2: fine-tuned Gemma-3 27B ranked third (overall 0.3571), BLIP achieved 0.3564, and zero-shot MedGemma-4B reached 0.3186.
AI.conclusion: A fine-tuned ensemble achieves state-of-the-art concept detection, while a training-free retrieval baseline provides a highly cost-effective near-equivalent alternative. For captioning, stronger fine-tuned models outperform zero-shot approaches, demonstrating a clear trade-off between model scale, training cost, and performance.

title: Private Face Recognition Training Dataset Publication via Identity-Decoupled and Geometry-Preserving Face Distillation
summary: Publishing private face recognition~(FR) training datasets is privacy-sensitive because faces expose identity information. Private FR training dataset publication mitigates this risk by releasing protected proxies as substitutes for private training faces. However, training FR models with such data introduces an identity paradox: \emph{the identity cues that make released faces useful for recognition supervision are also the cues that make them linkable to real individuals.} A protected face should be decoupled from the original identity, yet still behave as a reliable identity sample for training. Removing these cues too aggressively may destroy the class structure needed for recognition learning, whereas preserving them too faithfully may increase source-identity linkability. We argue that this paradox stems from conflating source-aligned identity semantics with recognition-useful proxy identity geometry. The former should be suppressed to reduce linkage to private individuals, while the latter should be preserved for FR learning. Based on this insight, we propose \textbf{Private Face Distillation}, an identity-decoupling and geometry-preserving framework. It uses Orthogonal Geometry Preservation to construct decoupled proxy identities from private identity representations while maintaining hyperspherical geometry, and Relational Topology Alignment to preserve identity relations for recognition learning. Experiments across multiple domain-shifted FR scenarios show that Private Face Distillation achieves stronger utility than the evaluated publication baselines. On IJB-C surveillance, it improves $\mathrm{TAR}@\mathrm{FAR}{=}1\text{e-}{3}$ by 3.94\% over the baseline while reducing source-identity linkability. These results suggest that private FR training dataset publication should decouple source-identity correspondence while preserving proxy identity geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Private Face Distillation (PFD), a framework for publishing privacy-preserving face recognition training datasets. It decouples source-identity semantics from recognition-useful proxy identity geometry, using Orthogonal Geometry Preservation and Relational Topology Alignment to reduce identity linkability while maintaining recognition utility.
AI.motivation: Private face recognition training dataset publication faces an identity paradox: identity cues needed for recognition supervision are the same cues that make faces linkable to real individuals. Existing approaches either over-suppress identity cues (destroying class structure) or over-preserve them (increasing identity linkability). The authors argue this paradox stems from conflating source-aligned identity semantics (which should be suppressed) with recognition-useful proxy identity geometry (which should be preserved).
AI.method: The framework has two key components: (1) Orthogonal Geometry Preservation, which constructs decoupled proxy identities from private identity representations while maintaining hyperspherical geometry; and (2) Relational Topology Alignment, which preserves identity relations necessary for recognition learning. Together these decouple source-identity correspondence while preserving proxy identity geometry.
AI.result: On IJB-C surveillance benchmark, the method improves TAR@FAR=1e-3 by 3.94% over the baseline while simultaneously reducing source-identity linkability. Experiments across multiple domain-shifted FR scenarios demonstrate stronger utility than evaluated publication baselines.
AI.conclusion: Private FR training dataset publication should decouple source-identity correspondence while preserving proxy identity geometry. The proposed PFD framework demonstrates that this approach achieves both better recognition utility and stronger privacy protection compared to existing baselines.

title: CXR-Retrieve: Compositional Text-to-Image Retrieval in Chest Radiography
summary:
Large chest radiography archives are difficult to search because most studies are paired only with free-text reports rather than structured clinical annotations. Vision-language models offer a natural interface for text-to-image retrieval, but current biomedical models are primarily optimized for report-to-image matching rather than for satisfying short clinical search queries. This creates an objective mismatch: a model may retrieve images related to words in the query while failing to satisfy the full clinical constraint, especially for conjunctions and negations such as ``atelectasis and no pneumonia.''
  We introduce CXR-Retrieve, a structured benchmark for compositional chest X-ray text-to-image retrieval. The benchmark contains 5,159 test images from the official test-split of MIMIC-CXR-JPG and 145 textual queries spanning single and conjunction findings, both positive and negative. Relevance is defined by whether a retrieved image satisfies all asserted pathology constraints, rather than by whether it matches a paired report.
  We further propose a label-aware contrastive fine-tuning objective for clinical retrieval. Our method attracts image-text pairs with compatible asserted pathology constraints, including shared confirmed absences, while explicitly repelling contradictory pairs. Starting from the in-domain CXR-CLIP checkpoint, our method improves Precision@5 over CXR-CLIP by 8.5 percentage points on two-pathology conjunctions and by 22.0 percentage points on negation queries. These results show that reliable chest X-ray retrieval requires training objectives that model not only which findings are mentioned, but also how they are clinically asserted.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces CXR-Retrieve, a structured benchmark for compositional chest X-ray text-to-image retrieval with 5,159 test images and 145 queries covering conjunctions and negations, plus a label-aware contrastive fine-tuning objective that improves retrieval precision by modeling clinical assertion semantics (confirmed vs. negated findings).
AI.motivation: Large chest radiography archives are hard to search because studies are paired with free-text reports rather than structured annotations. Existing biomedical vision-language models are optimized for full report-image matching, creating an objective mismatch: they may retrieve images matching query words while failing to satisfy full clinical constraints, especially for conjunctions and negations (e.g., "atelectasis and no pneumonia").
AI.method: The authors (1) build CXR-Retrieve, a benchmark with 5,159 MIMIC-CXR-JPG test images and 145 queries spanning single/conjunction findings with positive and negative assertions, where relevance is defined by whether an image satisfies all asserted pathology constraints. (2) Propose a label-aware contrastive fine-tuning objective that attracts image-text pairs with compatible asserted pathology constraints (including shared confirmed absences) while repelling contradictory pairs.
AI.result: Starting from the in-domain CXR-CLIP checkpoint, the method improves Precision@5 over CXR-CLIP by 8.5 percentage points on two-pathology conjunctions and by 22.0 percentage points on negation queries.
AI.conclusion: Reliable chest X-ray retrieval requires training objectives that model not only which findings are mentioned, but also how they are clinically asserted (confirmed vs. negated), demonstrating that label-aware compositional reasoning is essential for clinical retrieval performance.

title: FDDWAN: A Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Network for Watermarking Attack
summary: Existing invisible watermark removal methods often struggle to accurately capture the watermark-bearing features, leading to an unfavorable trade-off between watermark suppression and perceptual fidelity. In this paper, we propose the Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Watermark Attack Network (FDDWAN), a coarse-to-fine framework that performs watermark removal through wavelet-domain decomposition and residual diffusion refinement. In the initial stage, the Wavelet-based Frequency-domain Preliminary Attack Module (WFPAM) decomposes the watermarked image into low- and high-frequency subbands and applies frequency-specific attack strategies tailored to their respective contributions to watermark robustness and perceptual quality. In the next stage, the Frequency-domain Residual Diffusion Attack Module (FRDAM) separately models the residual distributions between the preliminarily attacked outputs and the corresponding watermark-free references during training. Rather than reconstructing the entire image, FRDAM selectively refines frequency-domain residuals, directing the diffusion process toward the remaining watermark related discrepancies while minimizing modifications to image content. Extensive experiments on CelebA and ImageNet across four representative watermarking schemes demonstrate that FDDWAN achieves a more favorable trade-off between watermark removal effectiveness and visual fidelity than conventional and learning-based attack methods.

AI.tldr: FDDWAN is a coarse-to-fine diffusion-based framework for invisible watermark removal that decomposes images in the wavelet domain and selectively refines frequency-domain residuals to balance watermark suppression and perceptual fidelity.
AI.motivation: Existing watermark removal methods struggle to capture watermark-bearing features accurately, resulting in an unfavorable trade-off between suppressing the watermark and preserving image quality.
AI.method: The framework has two stages: (1) WFPAM decomposes the watermarked image into low- and high-frequency subbands via wavelet transform and applies frequency-specific attack strategies; (2) FRDAM models residual distributions between preliminary outputs and watermark-free references, selectively refining frequency-domain residuals to direct diffusion toward remaining watermark discrepancies while minimizing content modification.
AI.result: Experiments on CelebA and ImageNet across four watermarking schemes show FDDWAN achieves a more favorable trade-off between watermark removal effectiveness and visual fidelity than conventional and learning-based attacks.
AI.conclusion: Frequency-domain decomposition combined with residual diffusion refinement enables superior watermark removal while maintaining perceptual quality.

title: LoMeVQA: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Longitudinal Medical VQA
comment: 23 pages, 17 figures, 7 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/pepperbubble/LoMeVQA
summary: In clinical practice, patients often undergo multiple imaging examinations over successive visits, yielding longitudinal data. Modeling such temporal information is crucial for reliable assessment of disease progression and treatment response. However, despite the rapid advancement of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), longitudinal medical visual reasoning remains largely underexplored. To fill this gap, we propose LoMeVQA, a comprehensive benchmark consisting of 206K longitudinal visual question answering (VQA) pairs for temporal medical image analysis. LoMeVQA covers five tasks: progress classification, progress description, progress report generation, differential region grounding, and differential region description. To construct the dataset, we develop an automated pipeline that (1) organizes patient records chronologically, (2) extracts clinically meaningful entities via a medical knowledge graph, and (3) models their temporal evolution to guide large language models in generating high-quality longitudinal VQA pairs. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that both general-purpose and medical-domain MLLMs perform poorly on LoMeVQA, revealing substantial limitations in temporal reasoning. To address these limitations, we introduce MedLong-8B, which achieves state-of-the-art performance across all tasks. Beyond benchmarking, we conduct detailed analyses that uncover key failure modes and shed light on how to improve longitudinal medical visual reasoning. Our data is available at: https://github.com/pepperbubble/LoMeVQA

AI.tldr: This paper introduces LoMeVQA, a benchmark of 206K longitudinal medical visual QA pairs spanning five temporal reasoning tasks, along with MedLong-8B, an 8B model achieving state-of-the-art performance after showing that existing MLLMs perform poorly on temporal medical reasoning.
AI.motivation: Patients accumulate longitudinal imaging data over successive visits, and modeling temporal information is essential for assessing disease progression and treatment response. Despite advances in multimodal large language models, longitudinal medical visual reasoning remains largely underexplored, creating a significant gap in both benchmarks and model capability.
AI.method: The authors propose LoMeVQA with 206K VQA pairs covering five tasks (progress classification, progress description, progress report generation, differential region grounding, differential region description). They build an automated pipeline that chronologically organizes patient records, extracts clinically meaningful entities via a medical knowledge graph, models their temporal evolution, and uses LLMs to generate high-quality longitudinal VQA pairs. They also introduce MedLong-8B for improved temporal reasoning.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations show both general-purpose and medical-domain MLLMs perform poorly on LoMeVQA, revealing substantial limitations in temporal reasoning. MedLong-8B achieves state-of-the-art performance across all tasks. Detailed analysis uncovers key failure modes and insights for improving longitudinal medical visual reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The work fills a critical gap in longitudinal medical visual reasoning by providing a comprehensive benchmark and a strong baseline model, while offering analysis that illuminates how to improve temporal reasoning in medical MLLMs moving forward.

title: SPFM-Net: Semantic-Prior-Guided Frequency-Constrained Mamba for Invisible Watermark Attack
summary: Existing watermark attacks typically rely on predefined signal-processing operations or locally constrained restoration networks, making it difficult to capture the long-range dependencies of globally distributed watermark signals and resulting in an unfavorable trade-off between removal effectiveness and visual fidelity. In this paper, we propose SPFM-Net, a semantic-prior-guided and frequency-constrained Mamba framework for invisible watermark attack. SPFM-Net first employs high-ratio masking to disrupt the spatial coherence of invisible watermark signals, and then utilizes a partially fine-tuned pretrained Masked Autoencoder to reconstruct semantically consistent image from sparse observations while suppressing watermark-related information. A Multi-scale Residual Frequency Feature Interaction module subsequently aggregates watermark-related residual features across multiple receptive fields, while adaptively suppressing responses from watermark-irrelevant regions. To further capture the long-range dependencies of globally distributed watermark signals, a lightweight Mamba-based Global State-space Feature Modeling (GSFM) unit is introduced to separate watermark-related features from natural image content and suppress the remaining watermark traces. In addition, SPFM-Net is optimized using a multi-level objective that jointly imposes spatial-, frequency-, and edge-domain constraints, enabling effective watermark suppression while preserving perceptual quality. Extensive experiments on representative spatial-domain, transform-domain, orthogonal moment-based, and deep learning-based watermarking schemes demonstrate that SPFM-Net achieves a favorable trade-off between watermark attack effectiveness and perceptual fidelity.

AI.tldr: SPFM-Net is a semantic-prior-guided and frequency-constrained Mamba framework for invisible watermark attacks, combining high-ratio masking, a partially fine-tuned MAE, multi-scale residual frequency feature interaction, and a Mamba-based global state-space modeling unit to capture long-range dependencies of globally distributed watermark signals while achieving a favorable trade-off between attack effectiveness and visual fidelity.
AI.motivation: Existing watermark attacks rely on predefined signal-processing operations or locally constrained restoration networks, which fail to capture long-range dependencies of globally distributed watermark signals, resulting in poor trade-offs between removal effectiveness and visual fidelity.
AI.method: SPFM-Net consists of four key components: (1) high-ratio masking to disrupt watermark signal spatial coherence, (2) a partially fine-tuned pretrained Masked Autoencoder for semantic-consistent reconstruction and watermark suppression, (3) a Multi-scale Residual Frequency Feature Interaction module to aggregate watermark-related residual features across multiple receptive fields while suppressing irrelevant regions, and (4) a lightweight Mamba-based Global State-space Feature Modeling (GSFM) unit to capture long-range dependencies and separate watermark features from image content. The network is optimized with a multi-level objective enforcing spatial-, frequency-, and edge-domain constraints.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across spatial-domain, transform-domain, orthogonal moment-based, and deep learning-based watermarking schemes demonstrate that SPFM-Net achieves a favorable trade-off between watermark attack effectiveness and perceptual fidelity.
AI.conclusion: The proposed SPFM-Net effectively addresses the limitations of existing watermark attack methods by leveraging semantic priors, frequency constraints, and Mamba-based global modeling to achieve superior watermark removal while preserving image quality.

title: Hallucinations Leave a Grounding Signature:Verifier-Guided Decoding for Selective Object Correction
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) often hallucinate objects that are absent from an image. Despite recent progress, existing mitigation methods still lack reliable object-level grounding diagnostics and therefore tend to apply coarse-grained interventions, which can impair visual understanding, shorten responses, and reduce coverage of genuinely grounded objects. The key challenge is thus to detect, during generation, whether each emerging object mention is supported by reliable visual evidence, so that hallucination can be mitigated selectively. Yet output confidence reflects next-token plausibility rather than visual support, allowing language priors to make absent objects appear certain. We show that the missing diagnostic evidence is encoded in an Intrinsic Grounding Signature (IGS), a distributed signed attention pattern that remains informative for such confident hallucinations. Based on IGS, we propose Verifier-Guided Decoding (VGD), a decoding framework in which a lightweight verifier examines each emerging object mention, rolls back the KV cache when the mention is identified as high risk, suppresses the object and its synonyms, and regenerates the affected continuation. Because VGD intervenes only on object mentions identified as high risk, it reduces object hallucination while preserving the model's original visual understanding and grounded object coverage. Experiments on CHAIR and AMBER-G show that VGD achieves state-of-the-art object hallucination reduction: at @rec90, it cuts AMBER-G CHAIR by 43.6\% while retaining 99.6\% of grounded-object coverage, and reduces CHAIR-MSCOCO CHAIR$_i$/CHAIR$_s$ by 37.0\%/30.4\% without shortening captions.

AI.tldr: LVLMs hallucinate absent objects. The paper introduces Intrinsic Grounding Signature (IGS), a distributed signed attention pattern that encodes diagnostic evidence for grounding even in confident hallucinations. Based on IGS, they propose Verifier-Guided Decoding (VGD), a decoding framework that selectively rolls back KV cache and suppresses high-risk object mentions. VGD achieves SOTA hallucination reduction while preserving grounded-object coverage and caption length.
AI.motivation: Existing hallucination mitigation methods lack reliable object-level grounding diagnostics, applying coarse-grained interventions that impair visual understanding, shorten responses, and reduce coverage of genuinely grounded objects. The key challenge is detecting whether each emerging object mention is supported by reliable visual evidence during generation, since output confidence reflects next-token plausibility rather than visual support, allowing language priors to make absent objects appear certain.
AI.method: The paper shows that missing diagnostic evidence is encoded in an Intrinsic Grounding Signature (IGS), a distributed signed attention pattern informative even for confident hallucinations. Based on IGS, they propose Verifier-Guided Decoding (VGD), where a lightweight verifier examines each emerging object mention, rolls back the KV cache when the mention is high risk, suppresses the object and its synonyms, and regenerates the affected continuation. VGD intervenes only on high-risk object mentions.
AI.result: On CHAIR and AMBER-G, VGD achieves state-of-the-art object hallucination reduction: at @rec90, it cuts AMBER-G CHAIR by 43.6% while retaining 99.6% of grounded-object coverage, and reduces CHAIR-MSCOCO CHAIR_i/CHAIR_s by 37.0%/30.4% without shortening captions.
AI.conclusion: IGS provides reliable object-level grounding diagnostics, enabling selective intervention that reduces hallucination while preserving visual understanding and grounded-object coverage. VGD demonstrates that precise, targeted decoding interventions can outperform coarse-grained mitigation approaches.

title: Thinking Once Is Enough: Intermediate-Layer Evidence Routing for High-Resolution VQA
summary: High-resolution visual question answering (HR-VQA) is often treated as a problem of insufficient evidence acquisition, where failing multimodal large language models must inspect images again through cropping, re-encoding, or multi-round search. We show that this view is incomplete: in many cases, fine-grained evidence has already survived visual encoding and become identifiable and influential within an intermediate-layer routing window, but is later diluted before answer generation. We propose Thinking-Once, a \textbf{training-free, single-visual-pass} evidence-routing method that reconstructs question-conditioned attention at this window, preserves core entity tokens and compact background context, and routes this evidence to later layers without extra visual encoding. Across five base models, Thinking-Once consistently improves or matches the corresponding base setting, increasing the average scores on V$^*$Bench, HRBench-4K, and HRBench-8K by \textit{+3.1}, \textit{+3.0}, and \textit{+2.7} points while reducing the average peak memory by about 4,GB. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, it improves the three benchmarks by \textit{+9.9}, \textit{+4.6}, and \textit{+5.5} points, raising the cross-benchmark mean from 72.5 to 79.1. With the ZwZ-8B base model, Thinking-Once reaches a mean score of 82.7. Against 11 open-source HR-VQA baselines, it obtains the best or tied-best score on all three benchmark averages and the best overall mean; for example, compared with DeepScan, it reduces V$^*$Bench inference time by \textbf{97.2\%} while improving the cross-benchmark mean from 77.8 to 79.1. These results show that HR-VQA can be improved by routing already encoded evidence rather than repeatedly acquiring new visual inputs. Code is available in the appendix.

AI.tldr: Thinking-Once is a training-free, single-visual-pass method for high-resolution visual question answering that routes question-conditioned attention from intermediate layers to later layers, preserving fine-grained evidence that was already encoded but diluted before answer generation. It improves performance across five base models and three benchmarks while reducing memory usage and inference time.
AI.motivation: The paper argues that HR-VQA is typically treated as an insufficient evidence acquisition problem, where models need to re-inspect images via cropping, re-encoding, or multi-round search. The authors show this view is incomplete: fine-grained evidence often already survives visual encoding and is identifiable in intermediate-layer routing windows, but gets diluted before answer generation. This challenges the need for repeated visual encoding.
AI.method: Thinking-Once reconstructs question-conditioned attention at an intermediate-layer routing window, preserves core entity tokens and compact background context, and routes this evidence to later layers—all without extra visual encoding and without training. It is a training-free, single-visual-pass evidence-routing approach.
AI.result: Across five base models, Thinking-Once consistently improves or matches baselines, increasing average scores on V*Bench, HRBench-4K, and HRBench-8K by +3.1, +3.0, and +2.7 points, respectively, while reducing average peak memory by ~4GB. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, it improves the three benchmarks by +9.9, +4.6, and +5.5 points (mean from 72.5 to 79.1). With ZwZ-8B, it reaches a mean of 82.7. Against 11 HR-VQA baselines, it achieves the best or tied-best score on all benchmark averages and reduces inference time by 97.2% compared to DeepScan while improving the cross-benchmark mean from 77.8 to 79.1.
AI.conclusion: HR-VQA can be improved by routing already-encoded evidence rather than repeatedly acquiring new visual inputs, demonstrating that the bottleneck is evidence dilution rather than evidence acquisition.

title: SAFViT: Spatial Attention Fusion Gating for Vision Transformer-Based Nucleus Segmentation and Classification
summary: Accurate cell segmentation and classification are foundational to digital pathology, enabling quantitative tissue analysis for diagnosis and treatment planning. Encoder-decoder architectures that fuse multi-scale features through skip connections have become the dominant paradigm for this task, yet standard direct skip connections treat every spatial location equally, which leads to redundant and potentially conflicting information reaching the decoder. To overcome this problem, various gating mechanisms have been introduced, but most of them operate solely on filtering encoder information, neglecting the benefit of global contextual information from the decoder. This study proposes replacing conventional skip connections in a CellViT-based model with a novel Spatial Attention Fusion (SAF) Gating module. Each SAF gate concatenates the encoder skip and upsampled decoder features, compresses them through two pointwise convolutions with an intermediate ReLU, and applies a channel-wise softmax to produce a per-pixel "heatmap of trust" that sums to unity at every spatial location, allowing the network to learn where each source is most trustworthy. The resulting fused features improve the model's ability to detect the minority "Dead" class, which in turn enhances the multi-class panoptic quality (mPQ) on the PanNuke dataset. SAF Gating is compared against six gating alternatives including no gating, attention gates, squeeze-and-excitation, CBAM, cross-attention, and attentional feature fusion on PanNuke and MoNuSeg datasets. SAF Gating achieves the highest mPQ (0.471), a gain driven primarily by a 14.5-point improvement in Dead-class F1 score compared to ungated CellViT baseline.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Spatial Attention Fusion (SAF) Gating module to replace conventional skip connections in a CellViT-based encoder-decoder model for cell segmentation and classification. The SAF gate fuses encoder skip and upsampled decoder features through pointwise convolutions and channel-wise softmax to produce per-pixel trust weighting. It achieves the highest mPQ (0.471) on PanNuke, driven mainly by a 14.5-point improvement in Dead-class F1 score over the baseline.
AI.motivation: Standard skip connections in encoder-decoder architectures treat all spatial locations equally, causing redundant or conflicting information to reach the decoder. Existing gating mechanisms only filter encoder information and neglect global contextual information from the decoder.
AI.method: The SAF Gating module replaces conventional skip connections in a CellViT-based model. Each gate concatenates encoder skip and upsampled decoder features, compresses them via two pointwise convolutions with intermediate ReLU, and applies channel-wise softmax to produce a per-pixel "heatmap of trust" summing to unity at each spatial location, letting the network learn source trustworthiness.
AI.result: SAF Gating achieves the highest mPQ (0.471) on the PanNuke dataset compared to six gating alternatives (no gating, attention gates, SE, CBAM, cross-attention, AFF) and MoNuSeg. The gain is primarily driven by a 14.5-point improvement in Dead-class F1 score over the ungated CellViT baseline.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating decoder context into gating via SAF improves multi-class panoptic segmentation quality, particularly for minority classes, demonstrating the value of bidirectional information flow in gated skip connections.

title: FeatFix: Reuse What You Verify through Local Exact-Feature Correction for Faster Cached Diffusion Inference
summary: Diffusion models are widely used to generate high-quality images and videos, but their iterative denoising process remains computationally intensive. A growing class of training-free accelerators reduces this cost by reusing cached intermediate features or forecasting future ones. To control draft drift, these methods sometimes compute an exact block feature for verification. Yet the resulting exact feature is typically used only to measure discrepancy or guide a later decision and is then discarded. We find that this previously computed feature can instead be reused for correction. Forwarding it at the verification site resets the local draft residual and reduces downstream feature error. Based on this observation, we introduce FeatFix, a local exact-feature correction method for cached diffusion inference. FeatFix operates at a fixed sparse set of layer--timestep sites. At each selected site, it replaces the complete draft block output with the exact output computed from the same incoming state, avoiding token- or channel-level partial replacement and full-timestep recomputation. Experiments across four image and video backbones show that FeatFix consistently accelerates generation, achieving a speedup of up to $6.70\times$ over Vanilla while maintaining competitive output quality.

AI.tldr: FeatFix is a training-free acceleration method for diffusion models that reuses exact features computed during verification to correct draft residuals at selected layer-timestep sites, achieving up to 6.70x speedup over Vanilla while maintaining output quality.
AI.motivation: Diffusion models are computationally intensive due to iterative denoising. Existing training-free accelerators cache or forecast intermediate features, and sometimes compute exact features for verification—but these exact features are discarded after serving a discrepancy check. The paper finds these previously computed features can be reused for correction to reduce downstream error.
AI.method: FeatFix operates at a fixed sparse set of layer-timestep sites. At each selected site, it replaces the complete draft block output with the exact output computed from the same incoming state, avoiding token/channel-level partial replacement and full-timestep recomputation. This corrects the local draft residual by forwarding the exact feature at the verification site.
AI.result: Experiments across four image and video backbones show FeatFix consistently accelerates generation, achieving speedup up to 6.70x over Vanilla while maintaining competitive output quality.
AI.conclusion: Reusing verification-computed exact features for local correction is an effective and simple strategy to improve cached diffusion inference, yielding significant speedups without full recomputation overhead.

title: VCP-DCN: Beyond Visual Concealed Property via Depth Collaborative Network for Camouflaged Object Detection
summary: Camouflaged Object Detection (COD) aims to identify and segment camouflaged objects in complex environments, which are often concealed because their color and texture are similar to the background. Several existing COD methods introduce depth maps to boost detection performance via learning complementary RGB-D features, ignoring modality-specific characteristics of concealed objects in the depth domain. To address this issue, we propose a depth collaborative network, called VCP-DCN, to mine distinguishable multi-modality features beyond visual concealed prototype in depth domain. Specifically, VCP-DCN progressively performs multi-modality alignment, interaction, and fusion for the COD task. In the \textbf{alignment} stage, we propose a Separable Prototype Embedding (SPE) module to learn modality-consistency and modality-specific RGB/depth prototype tokens through prototype contrastive learning. Furthermore, we develop a Multi-modality Dual Attention (MDA) module to enhance the cross-modal feature representation through local response maps between modality-consistency RGB/depth prototype tokens and visual tokens on the \textbf{interaction} stage. Finally, we design a Depth Adaptive Injection (DAI) module to adaptively measure contribution of RGB/depth features with a decision-making mechanism, which calculates similarity distance between RGB/depth modality-specific prototype tokens and modality-consistency ones on the \textbf{fusion} stage. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our VCP-DCN on three authoritative datasets.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes VCP-DCN, a depth collaborative network for Camouflaged Object Detection (COD) that mines distinguishable multi-modality features beyond visual concealed prototypes in the depth domain through progressive multi-modality alignment, interaction, and fusion stages.
AI.motivation: Existing COD methods that use depth maps simply learn complementary RGB-D features but ignore modality-specific characteristics of concealed objects in the depth domain, limiting detection performance.
AI.method: VCP-DCN performs three stages: (1) Alignment via a Separable Prototype Embedding (SPE) module that learns modality-consistency and modality-specific RGB/depth prototype tokens through prototype contrastive learning; (2) Interaction via a Multi-modality Dual Attention (MDA) module that enhances cross-modal feature representation using local response maps between modality-consistency prototype tokens and visual tokens; (3) Fusion via a Depth Adaptive Injection (DAI) module that adaptively measures RGB/depth feature contributions with a decision-making mechanism based on similarity distance between modality-specific and modality-consistency prototype tokens.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of VCP-DCN on three authoritative camouflaged object detection datasets.
AI.conclusion: The proposed depth collaborative network effectively mines distinguishable multi-modality features in the depth domain, achieving strong performance on COD benchmarks.

title: Benchmarking Foundation and Large Language Models for Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Few-shot medical image segmentation (FS-MIS) aims to segment novel regions of interest (ROIs) from a few annotated support examples. Despite rapid progress, existing FS-MIS solutions span diverse paradigms but are evaluated under inconsistent settings, leaving their relative effectiveness unclear. We introduce FAME, a unified benchmark for evaluating FS-MIS solutions, covering specialists, SAM-based methods, CLIP-based methods, and MLLM-based methods. FAME contains 14,958 test samples across 7 anatomical sites, 9 imaging modalities, and 14 ROI categories, and evaluates models under zero-shot and ten-shot settings with additional assessment of target-absence recognition and generalization under covariate and semantic shifts. Our evaluation reveals several findings. First, effective few-shot segmentation depends on how models exploit support examples: direct visual adaptation generally outperforms prompt-based strategies. Second, increasing support examples improves performance only when models can effectively utilize them. Third, semantic transfer remains substantially more challenging than imaging-domain adaptation, and strong localization ability does not necessarily imply reliable target-absence recognition. We hope FAME provides a comprehensive understanding of current FS-MIS solutions and facilitates the development of more effective and reliable few-shot medical segmentation methods.

AI.tldr: FAME is a unified benchmark for few-shot medical image segmentation (FS-MIS) covering 14,958 test samples across 7 anatomical sites, 9 imaging modalities, and 14 ROI categories, evaluating specialists, SAM-based, CLIP-based, and MLLM-based methods under zero-shot and ten-shot settings with assessments of target-absence recognition and generalization under covariate and semantic shifts.
AI.motivation: Existing FS-MIS solutions span diverse paradigms (specialists, SAM-based, CLIP-based, MLLM-based) but are evaluated under inconsistent settings, leaving their relative effectiveness unclear. A comprehensive unified benchmark is needed for fair comparison and insight generation.
AI.method: FAME provides a standardized evaluation framework covering multiple model paradigms, multiple imaging modalities and anatomical sites, evaluates under zero-shot and ten-shot settings, and includes additional assessments for target-absence recognition and robustness under covariate and semantic shifts.
AI.result: Three key findings: (1) direct visual adaptation of support examples outperforms prompt-based strategies; (2) adding more support examples only helps when models can effectively utilize them; (3) semantic transfer is more challenging than imaging-domain adaptation, and strong localization does not guarantee reliable target-absence recognition.
AI.conclusion: FAME provides a comprehensive understanding of current FS-MIS solutions and aims to facilitate the development of more effective and reliable few-shot medical segmentation methods.

title: EEG-EditBench: Probing Visual Information in EEG-Image Retrieval Models with Controlled Image Edits
comment: Main paper with supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/XiaoZhangYES/EEG-EditBench. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/xiaozgg/EEG-EditBench
summary: Recent EEG-to-image retrieval models have achieved strong performance in identifying viewed images from semantically diverse candidates. Yet such success does not reveal what visual information supports the match. A model may readily identify a cheetah among tools, plants, and vehicles, but can it still distinguish the viewed cheetah from the same scene with the cheetah replaced by a dog? Motivated by this question, we introduce EEG-EditBench, a diagnostic benchmark that examines this question through controlled edits of object identity, attributes, background, and object presence. Built from the 200 THINGS-EEG2 test images, EEG-EditBench contains 2,137 quality-controlled edits and evaluates eight representative EEG visual decoding models. Our results show that strong standard retrieval does not consistently transfer to edit-based evaluation, with fine-grained attribute changes presenting the greatest challenge. EEG-EditBench reveals model behavior hidden by aggregate retrieval accuracy and provides a controlled basis for studying what visual information EEG-image models preserve. The code and complete dataset are publicly available.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces EEG-EditBench, a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating EEG-to-image retrieval models by testing whether they can distinguish viewed images from controlled edits (object identity, attributes, background, object presence). Results show strong standard retrieval performance does not transfer to edit-based evaluation, with fine-grained attribute changes being most challenging.
AI.motivation: Existing EEG-to-image retrieval models achieve strong aggregate performance but it is unclear what specific visual information supports the match—e.g., whether a model identifies a cheetah because of global semantics or fine-grained visual detail. Standard retrieval accuracy can mask failures in distinguishing subtle visual differences.
AI.method: The authors build EEG-EditBench from 200 THINGS-EEG2 test images, creating 2,137 quality-controlled edits across four dimensions: object identity, attributes, background, and object presence. They evaluate eight representative EEG visual decoding models on this benchmark.
AI.result: Strong standard retrieval performance does not consistently transfer to edit-based evaluation. Fine-grained attribute changes present the greatest challenge to existing models, revealing behavior hidden by aggregate retrieval accuracy.
AI.conclusion: EEG-EditBench provides a controlled basis for studying what visual information EEG-image models actually preserve, and highlights the need for benchmarks that go beyond aggregate retrieval accuracy to diagnose model capabilities.

title: Learning to Understand Body Language from Flight through Robust 3D Avatar Placing
summary: Perceiving human motion and intent at long range is a prerequisite for socially intelligent aerial robots, yet the data to learn it barely exists. We introduce Drones2BodyLanguage, a dataset grounding human motion in real UAV footage: avatars manifesting ten communicative intents are placed into unmodified 4K drone scenes with metrically correct position, scale and orientation, maintained over hundreds of frames of camera motion. Enabling it is a lightweight geometric world model of the local scene - semantically selected anchors lifted to 3D through streaming monocular depth - in which a placement point is predicted as an affine anchor combination with provably rigid-invariant weights, and re-rendered under an SVD-fitted ground rotation. Across twelve architectures on scene- and motion-disjoint splits, training on placed data lifts mean intent accuracy by a wide margin for real, retargeted and generated motion alike, with gains confirmed on two in-the-wild scenes.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Drones2BodyLanguage, a dataset that places avatars with communicative intents into real 4K UAV footage using a geometric world model with affine anchor combinations and SVD-fitted ground rotations, demonstrating significant improvements in intent classification accuracy across twelve architectures.
AI.motivation: Perceiving human motion and intent at long range is essential for socially intelligent aerial robots, but there is a scarcity of training data grounding human motion in real drone footage.
AI.method: The method constructs a lightweight geometric world model of local scenes using semantically selected anchors lifted to 3D via streaming monocular depth. A placement point is predicted as an affine anchor combination with rigid-invariant weights, and avatars are re-rendered under an SVD-fitted ground rotation into unmodified 4K drone scenes with metrically correct position, scale, and orientation maintained over hundreds of frames.
AI.result: Across twelve architectures on scene- and motion-disjoint splits, training on placed data lifts mean intent accuracy by a wide margin for real, retargeted, and generated motion alike, with gains confirmed on two in-the-wild scenes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed dataset and placement methodology effectively bridge the gap between synthetic human motion data and real UAV footage, enabling improved long-range human intent perception for aerial robots.

title: DECODE: Tackling Representation and Decision Degradation in Continual AI-Generated Image Detection
summary: As generative models continue to evolve, AI-generated image detectors must incrementally adapt to emerging generative domains while preserving knowledge acquired from previous ones. This continual learning setting is particularly challenging because forensic traces are often subtle and generator-specific, making detectors highly vulnerable to catastrophic forgetting. Existing methods primarily address this problem by stabilizing feature representations, implicitly treating forgetting as a representation-level issue. In this paper, we show that this perspective is incomplete. We demonstrate that even when feature representations remain discriminative, the decision boundary can progressively drift as the classification head is continually optimized on new domains. These two effects jointly give rise to a compound failure mode, termed Dual Degradation. To overcome this challenge, we propose DECODE, a decoupled continual detection framework that jointly mitigates representation- and decision-level forgetting. Specifically, we introduce Subspace Diversity Regularization (SDR) to preserve diverse forensic representations and Closed-Form Decision Alignment (CDA) to recalibrate the shared classification head after each adapter merge without manual hyperparameter tuning. Extensive experiments on 19 generative domains show that DECODE achieves an average accuracy of 99.36% with only 0.39% forgetting, while further generalizing to 11 unseen generators with 95.36% accuracy.

AI.tldr: DECODE is a decoupled continual learning framework for AI-generated image detection that addresses both representation-level and decision-level forgetting (termed Dual Degradation), achieving 99.36% average accuracy with only 0.39% forgetting across 19 generative domains and generalizing to 11 unseen generators.
AI.motivation: Existing continual learning methods for AI image detectors treat catastrophic forgetting purely as a representation-level issue by stabilizing features. However, this perspective is incomplete because even with discriminative features, the decision boundary can drift as the classification head is continuously optimized on new domains, creating a compound failure mode called Dual Degradation.
AI.method: DECODE employs two key components: (1) Subspace Diversity Regularization (SDR) to preserve diverse forensic representations, and (2) Closed-Form Decision Alignment (CDA) to recalibrate the shared classification head after each adapter merge without requiring manual hyperparameter tuning, jointly addressing representation- and decision-level forgetting.
AI.result: On 19 generative domains, DECODE achieves 99.36% average accuracy with only 0.39% forgetting, and further generalizes to 11 unseen generators with 95.36% accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The paper demonstrates that continual AI-generated image detection requires addressing both representation-level and decision-level forgetting simultaneously, and DECODE provides an effective decoupled framework that achieves state-of-the-art performance with minimal forgetting and strong generalization to unseen generators.

title: Unifying Adversarially Robust Model Experts in Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs), such as CLIP, are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, posing a serious problem for real-life applications and deployment. Adversarial fine-tuning emerges as a prominent defense method; however, different fine-tuning strategies often produce specialized models with distinct robustness characteristics. Each fine-tuned model in turn thrives in some evaluation settings but falters on others, limiting their defensive capabilities. We refer to these specialized fine-tuned models as robust model experts and propose a collaborative adversarial fine-tuning framework: CARE - Collaborative Adversarial Robustness fine-tuning using Embedding alignment. CARE maintains multiple experts during training, enables knowledge exchange through embedding-space harmonization, and consolidates the learned knowledge into a single unified robust model. Experts benefit from one another while preserving their individual specializations, enabling the final model to inherit complementary robustness properties. In this paper, we demonstrate CARE on two different adversarial fine-tuning strategies with complementary robustness behaviors. Extensive experiments on classic image classification and downstream vision-language tasks display the effectiveness of our approach, with CARE being able to outperform individually learned model experts. The results suggest that collaborative learning across model experts is a promising direction for improving adversarial robustness.

AI.tldr: CARE is a collaborative adversarial fine-tuning framework that trains multiple specialized robust model experts, harmonizes their knowledge through embedding-space alignment, and consolidates them into a single unified model that inherits complementary robustness properties.
AI.motivation: Different adversarial fine-tuning strategies produce specialized models (robust model experts) that each excel in some evaluation settings but fail in others. No single expert provides comprehensive robustness, limiting defensive capabilities in real-world VLM applications.
AI.method: CARE maintains multiple experts during training simultaneously, enables knowledge exchange via embedding-space harmonization, preserves each expert's individual specialization, and consolidates the learned knowledge into a single unified robust model.
AI.result: CARE outperforms individually learned model experts on classic image classification and downstream vision-language tasks, demonstrating that collaborative learning improves adversarial robustness.
AI.conclusion: Collaborative fine-tuning across robust model experts is a promising direction for improving adversarial robustness, as combining complementary specialization yields a stronger unified defense model.

title: CoRE-UIR: Prior-guided common and residual experts for efficient all-in-one remote sensing image restoration
comment: Accepted by ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
summary: Remote sensing images acquired by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and satellites are often degraded by adverse weather, illumination variation, and imaging artifacts, which may co-occur and jointly induce global distribution shifts and local structural corruption. Although All-in-One image restoration offers an appealing unified alternative to task-specific pipelines, existing methods still suffer from weak or implicit degradation cues and parameter redundancy caused by full-rank multi-expert designs with overlapping restoration behaviors. We propose CoRE-UIR (Common and Residual Experts for Universal Image Restoration), a prior-guided global-local framework centered on the Common-and-Residual Expert Block (CoRE). CoRE explicitly decomposes restoration capacity into a common dense expert for degradation-invariant restoration and low-rank residual experts for degradation-specific compensation, enabling adaptive specialization without redundant expert replication. Built on this design, Degradation Prior Embedding (DPE) adapts frozen CLIP features into an explicit restoration-oriented prior, while Global Feature Modulation (GFM) aligns global feature statistics before local residual compensation. We also construct MDVD-108K (Multi-Degradation VisDrone), a large-scale UAV restoration dataset covering both single and compound degradations, together with a real-world test set. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets show that CoRE-UIR improves the overall average PSNR by 1.05 dB while running 11.83$\times$ faster and reducing peak memory by 85.3% relative to the strongest baseline, BaryIR, thereby maintaining a favorable quality-efficiency trade-off. Evaluations on downstream tasks and unseen degradation also validate the generalizability of CoRE-UIR. The code and dataset will be released at https://github.com/zzaiyan/CoRE-UIR.

AI.tldr: CoRE-UIR is a unified framework for restoring UAV/satellite remote sensing images degraded by multiple co-occurring factors. It decomposes restoration into a common dense expert for degradation-invariant features and low-rank residual experts for degradation-specific compensation, achieving +1.05 dB PSNR while being 11.83x faster and using 85.3% less memory than the strongest baseline. The paper also introduces MDVD-108K, a large-scale multi-degradation UAV dataset.
AI.motivation: Remote sensing images suffer from co-occurring degradations (weather, illumination, artifacts) that cause both global distribution shifts and local structural corruption. Existing All-in-One restoration methods use full-rank multi-expert designs with redundant and overlapping behaviors, while also lacking explicit degradation cues—motivating a more efficient and prior-guided unified approach.
AI.method: Proposes CoRE-UIR built on the Common-and-Residual Expert Block (CoRE), which decomposes capacity into a common dense expert for degradation-invariant restoration plus low-rank residual experts for degradation-specific compensation. Previously restored features are handled via Degradation Prior Embedding (DPE) with frozen CLIP, and Global Feature Modulation (GFM) aligns global statistics before local residual compensation. Also constructs MDVD-108K for training/evaluation.
AI.result: CoRE-UIR improves average PSNR by 1.05 dB, runs 11.83x faster, and reduces peak memory by 85.3% versus the strongest baseline BaryIR. It also shows strong generalization on downstream tasks and unseen degradations.
AI.conclusion: A prior-guided global-local decomposition of restoration capacity into common and residual experts yields both better quality and dramatically improved efficiency, with validated generalizability beyond the training degradation set.

title: One Patch Is Enough: Reinforcement-Optimized Visual Token Grounding for MLLM-Based Scene Text Spotting
comment: 15 pages, 11 figures. Accepted to ACM Multimedia 2026
summary: Scene text spotting requires high-precision alignment between textual recognition and spatial localization. While visual-token grounding has emerged as a promising formulation for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), the previous multi-patch paradigm often introduces redundant noise and localization ambiguity, particularly for dense or small text instances. To address this, we propose Single-Patch Text Spotting (SPaTS), a vision-centric framework that routes each text instance through a single anchor visual token and then recovers geometry via full-image refinement. To accurately identify this anchor without oracle labels, we introduce Single-Patch Selective Optimization (SPaSO), a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes discrete visual-token selection using patch-level rewards. To further improve representation robustness and localization precision, we introduce Directional Embedding Alignment (DEA) to suppress unstable norm bias by decoupling feature magnitude and direction, and Patch-Enhanced Decoding (PED) to fuse the routed anchor with language semantics and cross-attend over the full-image feature map for geometry-aware boundary regression beyond coordinate-space surrogates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SPaTS consistently and significantly outperforms both frontier closed-source MLLMs and OCR MLLMs. Code will be released soon.

AI.tldr: SPaTS is a vision-centric framework for scene text spotting that routes each text instance through a single anchor visual token, using reinforcement learning for anchor selection (SPaSO), directional embedding alignment for robust representations, and patch-enhanced decoding for precise geometry-aware boundary regression, outperforming frontier MLLMs.
AI.motivation: Previous multi-patch visual-token grounding paradigms for MLLM-based scene text spotting introduce redundant noise and localization ambiguity, especially for dense or small text instances, motivating a cleaner single-patch formulation.
AI.method: SPaTS routes each text instance through a single anchor visual token with full-image refinement for geometry recovery. It uses SPaSO, a reinforcement learning framework for optimizing discrete visual-token selection via patch-level rewards; DEA for decoupling feature magnitude and direction to suppress norm bias; and PED to fuse routed anchors with language semantics and cross-attend over full-image features for geometry-aware boundary regression.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show SPaTS consistently and significantly outperforms both frontier closed-source MLLMs and OCR MLLMs.
AI.conclusion: Single-patch visual-token routing with reinforcement learning-based anchor selection and geometry-aware decoding provides a superior alternative to multi-patch grounding for scene text spotting in MLLMs.

title: ARD-REFSM: Enhancing Reflection Symmetry Detection with Asymmetric Denoising and Rotation Equivariance
summary: Reflection symmetry detection remains challenging due to interference from asymmetric regions and arbitrary orientations of symmetric patterns. Asymmetric regions introduce background clutter that disrupts symmetric pattern matching, whereas conventional convolutional neural networks lack rotation equivariance, leading to inconsistent feature representations under rotational transformations. To address these issues, we propose an Asymmetric Region Denoising (ARD) module and a Rotation Equivariant Feature Similarity Matching (REFSM) module. The ARD module suppresses asymmetric interference to refine symmetric patterns, while the REFSM module enhances rotation equivariance through feature similarity matching between original and rotated images. Specifically, our dual-input REFSM framework leverages rotation loss to maximize consistency between the score maps of original and rotated images, thereby enabling precise prediction of rotation-equivariant symmetry axes. Furthermore, we introduce GMSYM, a new benchmark dataset that categorizes images into diverse scenarios and incorporates various interferences to address the limitations of existing reflection symmetry detection benchmarks. Extensive experiments on four standard datasets (DENDI, NYU, LDRS, SDRW) and our proposed GMSYM dataset demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both accuracy and robustness.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a reflection symmetry detection method combining an Asymmetric Region Denoising (ARD) module to suppress background clutter and a Rotation Equivariant Feature Similarity Matching (REFSM) module to handle arbitrary orientation via rotation loss between original and rotated images. A new benchmark dataset (GMSYM) is also introduced, achieving state-of-the-art results on DENDI, NYU, LDRS, SDRW, and GMSYM.
AI.motivation: Reflection symmetry detection is difficult because (1) asymmetric regions introduce background clutter that disrupts symmetric pattern matching, and (2) conventional CNNs lack rotation equivariance, producing inconsistent features under rotation. These two challenges hinder accurate detection of symmetric patterns at arbitrary orientations.
AI.method: The method comprises two key modules: (1) ARD module that suppresses asymmetric region interference to refine symmetric patterns; (2) REFSM module that uses a dual-input framework to perform feature similarity matching between original and rotated images and applies a rotation loss to maximize consistency between score maps, enabling rotation-equivariant symmetry axis prediction. A new dataset GMSYM with diverse scenarios and interferences is also introduced.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on four standard datasets (DENDI, NYU, LDRS, SDRW) and the proposed GMSYM dataset show state-of-the-art performance in both accuracy and robustness.
AI.conclusion: The combination of asymmetric region denoising and rotation equivariant feature matching effectively addresses background clutter and orientation issues in reflection symmetry detection, with the new GMSYM benchmark further supporting evaluation under diverse real-world scenarios.

title: LAST: The Last Query Token Guides Visual Token Pruning for Edge-Cloud Collaborative MLLM Inference
summary: Multimodal foundation models are reshaping edge-cloud visual intelligence from task-specific feature pipelines into token-based interfaces, where edge devices encode visual inputs into tokens for a general-purpose cloud MLLM. However, dense visual-token sequences increase cloud-side inference costs. Existing pruning methods mainly target centralized inference: vision-driven methods can operate before cloud execution but are typically query-agnostic, whereas query-guided methods often rely on internal states of the target MLLM and cannot determine token relevance before transmission. Compact guidance models offer an alternative, but existing designs may require costly attention aggregation or auxiliary generation. We propose LAST, a training-free framework for query-dependent visual token pruning in edge-cloud collaborative MLLM inference. LAST uses a compact edge-side VLM as a guidance proxy and derives a lightweight importance signal from the last query token's attention to visual tokens. Under causal attention, the last query token can attend to the full visual sequence and the entire query context, enabling query-aware pruning without cloud-model access, autoregressive generation, or costly aggregation over multiple query positions. LAST then retains a diverse set of query-relevant visual tokens under a fixed token budget. We evaluate LAST on 11 multimodal benchmarks under multiple token budgets against pruning methods with different guidance strategies. Experiments show that LAST consistently achieves the strongest performance, preserving 95.4% of the full-token accuracy while retaining only 12.5% of the visual tokens, with low edge-side selection overhead and reduced cloud-side computation.

AI.tldr: LAST is a training-free framework for query-dependent visual token pruning in edge-cloud collaborative MLLM inference, using a compact edge-side VLM as a guidance proxy to identify query-relevant visual tokens via the last query token's attention, achieving 95.4% of full-token accuracy while retaining only 12.5% of visual tokens.
AI.motivation: Edge-cloud visual intelligence is shifting to token-based interfaces where edge devices encode visual inputs into tokens for cloud MLLMs, but dense visual-token sequences increase cloud-side inference costs. Existing pruning methods struggle in this setting: vision-driven methods are query-agnostic, query-guided methods rely on cloud MLLM internals unavailable before transmission, and compact guidance models require costly attention aggregation or auxiliary generation.
AI.method: LAST uses a compact edge-side VLM as a guidance proxy and derives a lightweight importance signal from the last query token's attention to visual tokens. Under causal attention, the last query token attends to the full visual sequence and entire query context, enabling query-aware pruning without cloud-model access, autoregressive generation, or aggregation over multiple query positions. It retains a diverse set of query-relevant visual tokens under a fixed token budget.
AI.result: Evaluated on 11 multimodal benchmarks under multiple token budgets, LAST consistently achieves the strongest performance, preserving 95.4% of full-token accuracy while retaining only 12.5% of visual tokens, with low edge-side selection overhead and reduced cloud-side computation.
AI.conclusion: LAST demonstrates that effective query-dependent visual token pruning can be achieved in a training-free manner using a compact edge-side guidance proxy, enabling efficient edge-cloud collaborative MLLM inference without compromising accuracy.

title: FiRE: Enhancing MLLMs with Fine-Grained Context Learning for Complex Image Retrieval
summary: Due to their strong generalizable multimodal processing and reasoning capabilities, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated significant potential as universal image retrievers, effectively addressing diverse real-world image retrieval tasks. Nevertheless, pioneering studies, while promising, overlook the potential of fine-grained context modeling and disentangled fine-tuning objectives in enhancing MLLMs' retrieval performance, particularly for complex tasks such as long-text-to-image retrieval, visual dialog retrieval, and composed image retrieval (CIR). Therefore, in this work, we propose an automated fine-grained multimodal quintuple dataset construction pipeline and a novel two-stage fine-grained multimodal fine-tuning strategy. The dataset generation pipeline produces a comprehensive CIR dataset with fine-grained image captions and modification text, facilitating fine-grained context modeling. Beyond the previously entangled fine-tuning paradigm, our approach separates the fine-tuning process into two distinct stages: (1) fine-grained context reasoning-oriented fine-tuning and (2) fine-grained retrieval-oriented fine-tuning. These stages aim to sequentially enhance the model's context understanding and query-target alignment capabilities, thereby improving retrieval performance. Extensive experiments across five datasets encompassing diverse and complex image retrieval tasks demonstrate the remarkable superiority of our method over existing approaches in zero-shot retrieval settings, even with a more lightweight MLLM backbone compared to those methods.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a fine-grained multimodal quintuple dataset construction pipeline and a two-stage fine-tuning strategy (context reasoning-oriented and retrieval-oriented) to enhance MLLMs' performance on complex image retrieval tasks including long-text-to-image, visual dialog retrieval, and composed image retrieval.
AI.motivation: Existing MLLM-based retrieval approaches overlook fine-grained context modeling and disentangled fine-tuning objectives, limiting performance on complex retrieval tasks like long-text-to-image retrieval, visual dialog retrieval, and composed image retrieval.
AI.method: (1) An automated pipeline for constructing a fine-grained multimodal quintuple dataset with detailed image captions and modification text. (2) A two-stage fine-tuning strategy: stage one focuses on fine-grained context reasoning, and stage two focuses on fine-grained retrieval-oriented alignment, decoupling the previously entangled fine-tuning paradigm.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across five datasets covering diverse complex retrieval tasks show the method outperforms existing approaches in zero-shot retrieval settings, even with a lighter-weight MLLM backbone.
AI.conclusion: Fine-grained context modeling combined with disentangled two-stage fine-tuning significantly improves MLLMs' universal image retrieval capability, achieving state-of-the-art results efficiently.

title: FootprintNet: State-Transition-Guided Dynamic Footprint Learning for Multi-temporal Remote Sensing Change Detection
summary: Despite substantial progress in remote sensing multi-temporal change detection (MTCD), most existing MTCD methods still represent the dynamic process at each spatial location over the entire observation period using a single change category associated with the final observation. This implicit single-change assumption limits their ability to characterize regions of recurrent change closely related to human activities. To address this limitation, we introduce Urban Building Dynamics Detection (UBDD), which identifies building-change dynamic footprints, i.e., the temporal intervals in which changes occur, from multi-temporal imagery and produces pixel-wise classification masks. For regions undergoing two or more changes, UBDD introduces an independent multi-change class for unified representation, thereby enabling unified modeling of single- and multi-change processes. Furthermore, we propose FootprintNet, which abstracts building-change processes as interactions between latent states and actions, and imposes state-action transition constraints to guide the learning of causally coherent change trajectories. It further exploits temporal change-boundary cues to enhance feature contrast across boundary sides, thereby improving the discrimination among different dynamic footprints and enabling accurate detection of dynamic footprints. Moreover, we introduce the Building Change Dynamics Score (BCDS) to address the inability of conventional metrics to reflect the temporal proximity between predicted footprints and labels. It evaluates predictions according to their preservation of change semantics and temporal offsets from the corresponding labels. Extensive experiments on TSCD, MUDS, and WUSU demonstrate that FootprintNet outperforms current state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/zmoka-zht/FootprintNet.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Urban Building Dynamics Detection (UBDD) and FootprintNet to detect building-change dynamic footprints (temporal intervals of change) from multi-temporal remote sensing imagery, handling both single and multiple changes per location. It also proposes a new metric (BCDS) and outperforms SOTA on TSCD, MUDS, and WUSU.
AI.motivation: Existing MTCD methods assume a single change per location over the observation period, limiting their ability to characterize regions with recurrent changes (e.g., areas undergoing two or more changes), which are common in human activity.
AI.method: FootprintNet abstracts building-change processes as interactions between latent states and actions, imposes state-action transition constraints for causally coherent change trajectories, and exploits temporal change-boundary cues to enhance feature contrast across boundary sides. It introduces an independent multi-change class for unified representation of single- and multi-change processes, plus BCDS metric to account for temporal proximity between predictions and labels.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on TSCD, MUDS, and WUSU demonstrate that FootprintNet outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed UBDD paradigm and FootprintNet effectively overcome the single-change limitation by enabling detection of dynamic footprints for both single and multiple changes, with BCDS providing a more meaningful evaluation metric aligned with change semantics and temporal offsets.

title: Now You Have My Healthy Attention: A U-DiT for Brain-MRI Inpainting
summary: The ASNR-MICCAI BraTS Local Synthesis (Inpainting) task asks for the anatomically plausible completion of healthy brain tissue within a masked region of a T1-weighted MRI, providing a tumor-free anatomical reference for downstream analysis. As the task is scored by distortion metrics (SSIM, PSNR, MSE), we build a deterministic regression model and focus on giving it inductive biases tailored to inpainting. Our network follows the U-DiT principle of performing self-attention on a downsampled token grid: a volumetric encoder-decoder imports long-range context through a downsampled global self-attention block with three-dimensional rotary position embeddings, while convolutions and skip connections preserve high-frequency detail. Two ideas drive our results. First, we constrain the attention so that occluded ("void") tokens attend only to known-healthy tokens of the same volume, with a learned bias toward each query's contralateral homologue, forcing the completion to be inferred from observed anatomy rather than from other unknown regions. Second, we add a contralateral-symmetry input that supplies the mirrored healthy hemisphere as a patient-specific prior; since the brain is approximately bilaterally symmetric and lesions are typically unilateral, this prior improves the distortion metrics at matched structural similarity. On the official BraTS-2026 validation leaderboard our submission reaches a mean healthy-region SSIM of $0.864$, PSNR of $24.7$\,dB and MSE of $4.6{\times}10^{-3}$ over $219$ cases. We further analyse the residual smoothness inherent to distortion-optimal regression and discuss its implications for anatomical realism.

AI.tldr: A deterministic regression model for brain MRI inpainting (BraTS Local Synthesis task) that uses a U-DiT architecture with downsampled global self-attention, constrained attention allowing void tokens to attend only to known-healthy tissue (with contralateral bias), and a contralateral-symmetry input prior.
