Achieves SSIM 0.864, PSNR 24.7 dB, MSE 4.6×10⁻³ on the BraTS-2026 validation leaderboard.
AI.motivation: The task requires anatomically plausible completion of healthy brain tissue in masked T1-weighted MRI regions to serve as a tumor-free reference. Since scoring is based on distortion metrics, the authors aim to build a model with inductive biases tailored for inpainting rather than generic generative approaches.
AI.method: Uses a U-DiT network: a volumetric encoder-decoder with a downsampled global self-attention block employing 3D rotary position embeddings for long-range context, while convolutions and skip connections preserve high-frequency detail. Two key ideas: (1) constrained attention where void tokens attend only to known-healthy tokens of the same volume with a learned bias toward the contralateral homologue; (2) a contralateral-symmetry input providing the mirrored healthy hemisphere as a patient-specific prior.
AI.result: On the official BraTS-2026 validation leaderboard over 219 cases, the submission achieves mean healthy-region SSIM of 0.864, PSNR of 24.7 dB, and MSE of 4.6×10⁻³.
AI.conclusion: The paper further analyzes the residual smoothness inherent to distortion-optimal regression and discusses its implications for anatomical realism, suggesting that while distortion metrics are optimized, this may come at a cost to perceptual/anatomical realism.

title: ViP-Rig: Visual-Prompted Controllable Rigging
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. Zihan Qin and Mingze Sun contributed equally. Xianming Liu is the corresponding author
summary: Rigging is inherently task-dependent because the same mesh may require different skeletons and deformation behaviors across animation tasks. In practice, artists often inspect an initial rig and repeatedly edit its skeletal structure and deformation behavior to meet specific animation requirements. Existing automatic methods primarily generate a plausible rig from geometry, offering limited explicit control over the resulting skeleton and deformation behavior. In this work, we present ViP-Rig, a visual-prompted framework that supports both prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing by injecting features extracted from user-drawn or edited 2D skeletal and rigidity prompts into frozen pretrained backbones. Specifically, ViP-Rig consists of two stages, Skeleton Generation and Skinning Prediction. In the first stage, the skeletal sketch is processed by the Dense-to-Compact Visual Prompt Encoding to produce compact, fixed-length conditioning tokens. The resulting tokens are injected into a frozen pretrained autoregressive generator through gated adapters to control joint placement and branching structure while preserving the generator's geometric prior. In the second stage, the rigidity map is processed using the same visual encoding design, while the pretrained skinning backbone remains frozen. The resulting tokens are symmetrically injected into the point and joint streams to modulate point-joint compatibility and the resulting skinning weights. Experiments on Articulation-XL2.0 and zero-shot evaluation on ModelsResource show that ViP-Rig more accurately recovers target skeletons and skinning weights than geometry-conditioned baselines under prompt-guided evaluation. Qualitative results further demonstrate explicit and localized control in both prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing.

AI.tldr: ViP-Rig is a visual-prompted rigging framework that injects features from user-drawn 2D skeletal and rigidity prompts into frozen pretrained backbones, enabling both prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing with explicit control over skeleton structure and deformation behavior.
AI.motivation: Rigging is inherently task-dependent since the same mesh may need different skeletons and deformation behaviors across animation tasks. Existing automatic methods only generate plausible rigs from geometry without offering explicit user control over the resulting skeleton and deformation behavior, which artists need in practice.
AI.method: ViP-Rig has two stages: (1) Skeleton Generation, where a skeletal sketch is processed by Dense-to-Compact Visual Prompt Encoding to produce compact conditioning tokens injected into a frozen autoregressive generator via gated adapters for joint placement and branching; (2) Skinning Prediction, where a rigidity map is encoded similarly and tokens are symmetrically injected into point and joint streams of a frozen skinning backbone to modulate point-joint compatibility.
AI.result: Experiments on Articulation-XL2.0 and zero-shot evaluation on ModelsResource show ViP-Rig recovers target skeletons and skinning weights more accurately than geometry-conditioned baselines under prompt-guided evaluation, with qualitative results demonstrating explicit and localized control.
AI.conclusion: ViP-Rig provides a flexible visual-prompted framework that enables explicit control over rigging through user-drawn 2D prompts while preserving the geometric priors of frozen pretrained backbones, supporting both prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing workflows.

title: Deep learning-based hierarchical insect classification using camera trap imagery
summary: Declining insect populations make reliable biodiversity monitoring increasingly urgent, yet monitoring of insect biodiversity is hampered by a lack of standardised data and by costly and time-consuming manual identification by expert entomologists. Deep learning-based image classifiers, processing data from automated non-lethal camera traps, have the potential to transform and scale insect biodiversity monitoring. However, challenges remain in acquiring expert-annotated datasets, developing model architectures that generalise well across diverse taxonomic levels and training models on highly imbalanced data. Hierarchical data also benefits from designing models that default to higher-confidence, coarser-level predictions, when uncertain about finer taxonomic levels. In this paper we address these challenges with a deep learning-based hierarchical classification model. First, we present a manually curated, long-tailed dataset of around one million images of insects, extracted from 1,801 camera-trap video recordings and annotated with a five-level, 34-class hierarchy. Further, we adapt a hierarchical classification model architecture to a five-level variable-depth hierarchy, with class-balanced weighting. Our model improves on non-hierarchical classifiers by leveraging biological taxonomy to extract granularity-specific visual features and makes hierarchy-consistent predictions to the deepest taxonomic level that meets a confidence threshold (T = 0.6). Our model achieved a per-level accuracy of 80-99% on test data, across five levels of hierarchy. Furthermore ...

AI.tldr: A deep learning-based hierarchical classification model for insect biodiversity monitoring using camera trap imagery, trained on a manually curated long-tailed dataset of ~1 million insect images annotated with a 5-level, 34-class taxonomic hierarchy.
AI.motivation: Insect populations are declining, making biodiversity monitoring urgent, but current approaches are hampered by lack of standardized data and costly, time-consuming manual identification by expert entomologists.
AI.method: The authors present a curated long-tailed dataset of ~1 million insect images from 1,801 camera-trap videos with a 5-level, 34-class hierarchy, and adapt a hierarchical classification model with class-balanced weighting that extracts granularity-specific visual features based on biological taxonomy and makes hierarchy-consistent predictions to the deepest taxonomic level meeting a confidence threshold (T=0.6).
AI.result: The model achieved 80-99% per-level accuracy on test data across all five levels of hierarchy.
AI.conclusion: Hierarchical classification leveraging biological taxonomy improves insect biodiversity monitoring accuracy compared to non-hierarchical classifiers, enabling scalable automated monitoring through camera traps.

title: Beyond Classification: Pathology Foundation Models as Detection Encoders for Mitotic Figures
summary: Pathology foundation models (FMs) are models trained on vast amounts of typically unlabeled data and have been shown to yield regularized latent spaces that can be used effectively in downstream classification tasks. This is also true for the classification of mitotic figures vs. other cells. However, it is so far unclear if the latent space of current FMs provides features that are discriminant and spatially suitably resolved to also serve as a backbone for dense object detection paradigms. In this work, we investigate this question for common current pathology FMs (UNI, UNI2-h, Virchow, Virchow2, H-optimus-0, H-optimus-1) and compare their performance against a fully end-to-end trained baseline based on a ResNet50 architecture. We combine FM backbones with representatives of single stage, dual stage and self-attention-based detectors (RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, Deformable DETR respectively) on the multi-domain MIDOG++ dataset, and on the TUPAC16 dataset as an out-of-domain case. We show that the H-optimus-0 and Virchow models yielded competitive performance, indicating that the latent spaces of current FMs, all trained on image-level self-supervision, are suitable for direct mitotic figure detection and may be slightly more robust on our out-of-domain test case. All code is made available publicly at https://github.com/DeepMicroscopy/FM4MFdet.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether current pathology foundation models (FMs) provide suitably resolved and discriminant features to serve as backbones for dense object detection, specifically for mitotic figure detection. They compare six FMs (UNI, UNI2-h, Virchow, Virchow2, H-optimus-0, H-optimus-1) combined with three detector architectures (RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, Deformable DETR) against a ResNet50 baseline, finding H-optimus-0 and Virchow competitive on MIDOG++ and slightly more robust on out-of-domain TUPAC16.
AI.motivation: While pathology FMs are known to work well for image-level classification tasks like mitotic figure vs. other cell classification, it is unclear whether their latent spaces provide features that are sufficiently discriminant and spatially resolved for dense object detection tasks, which require localization in addition to classification.
AI.method: The authors combine six pathology FMs (UNI, UNI2-h, Virchow, Virchow2, H-optimus-0, H-optimus-1) with three detector types (single-stage RetinaNet, dual-stage Faster R-CNN, and self-attention-based Deformable DETR) as backbones. They evaluate on the multi-domain MIDOG++ dataset with TUPAC16 as an out-of-domain test case, comparing against a fully end-to-end trained ResNet50 baseline.
AI.result: H-optimus-0 and Virchow achieved competitive performance, demonstrating that current FM latent spaces trained via image-level self-supervision are suitable for direct mitotic figure detection, and the FM-based approaches were slightly more robust on the out-of-domain TUPAC16 test case.
AI.conclusion: The latent spaces of current pathology foundation models are suitable for dense object detection in mitotic figure detection tasks, providing competitive or slightly better robustness than end-to-end trained baselines, and the code is publicly released.

title: ENCORE: Event-Assisted Complementary Motion Refinement for Learned Video Compression
summary: Learned video compression relies on accurate temporal modeling to remove redundancy between adjacent frames. However, most existing codecs infer motion solely from discretely sampled RGB frames, making their estimates vulnerable to fast motion, blur, occlusion, weak texture, low illumination, and abrupt brightness changes. Event cameras asynchronously capture fine-grained intensity changes between RGB timestamps and therefore provide complementary evidence about inter-frame dynamics. We propose ENCORE, an Event-Assisted Complementary Motion Refinement framework for learned video compression. ENCORE first employs Complementary Motion Representation (CMR) to decompose aligned RGB-event features into common and modality-specific motion representations. Spatial Energy and Redundancy-Informed Calibration (SERIC) then identifies event-specific responses that are active and novel relative to RGB, suppresses weak or redundant evidence, and predicts a candidate flow correction. Finally, Energy-Aware Routing (EAR) determines where and how strongly the correction should refine the RGB flow. Events serve solely as an auxiliary modality for motion modeling, while RGB remains the only coding and reconstruction target. Experiments on BS-ERGB, HQ-EVFI, and CED demonstrate consistent gains across datasets and GOP lengths. On BS-ERGB, ENCORE achieves up to 20.80% PSNR-RGB and 22.14% MS-SSIM-RGB BD-rate savings, while retaining clear improvements on the other two datasets.

AI.tldr: ENCORE is a framework that uses event cameras as an auxiliary modality to refine motion estimation in learned video compression, improving performance on challenging scenarios like fast motion and occlusion.
AI.motivation: Existing learned video codecs estimate motion from discretely sampled RGB frames, which fails under fast motion, blur, occlusion, weak texture, low illumination, and brightness changes. Event cameras asynchronously capture intensity changes between frames and can provide complementary motion evidence.
AI.method: ENCORE uses three components: (1) Complementary Motion Representation (CMR) decomposes aligned RGB-event features into common and modality-specific representations; (2) Spatial Energy and Redundancy-Informed Calibration (SERIC) identifies active and novel event-specific responses, suppresses weak/redundant evidence, and predicts a candidate flow correction; (3) Energy-Aware Routing (EAR) decides where and how strongly to refine the RGB flow. Events are auxiliary; RGB remains the only coding target.
AI.result: On BS-ERGB, ENCORE achieves up to 20.80% PSNR-RGB and 22.14% MS-SSIM-RGB BD-rate savings, with consistent gains across BS-ERGB, HQ-EVFI, and CED datasets and varying GOP lengths.
AI.conclusion: Event-assisted complementary motion refinement consistently improves learned video compression across multiple datasets, demonstrating that event data can effectively serve as an auxiliary modality for robust motion modeling without changing the RGB coding target.

title: Split and Drive: Dual-Axis Disentanglement for Real-Time Gaussian Head Avatars
summary: Creating photorealistic animatable head avatars from a single image remains a fundamental challenge in digital human synthesis. While recent 3D Gaussian Splatting methods have achieved promising results, they rely on external tracking pipelines whose latency is excluded from inference measurements. Furthermore, they adopt unified representations that entangle geometrically distinct facial regions, limiting both expressiveness and rendering fidelity. We propose SpiD (Split and Drive), a single-image Gaussian head avatar framework built on two disentanglement axes. The compute axis internalizes per-frame driving, eliminating external tracking dependency at inference. The feature axis decomposes the avatar into three specialized Gaussian branches, each modeling a geometrically distinct facial domain. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistently strong performance against state-of-the-art methods while achieving the fastest inference speed among all compared methods on a single GPU with the complete driving pipeline included.

AI.tldr: SpiD (Split and Drive) is a single-image Gaussian head avatar framework that disentangles along two axes: internalizing per-frame driving to eliminate external tracking dependency at inference, and decomposing the avatar into three specialized Gaussian branches for geometrically distinct facial regions, achieving state-of-the-art performance with the fastest inference speed on a single GPU.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting head avatar methods rely on external tracking pipelines whose latency is excluded from inference measurements (unfair and impractical), and they use unified representations that entangle geometrically distinct facial regions, limiting expressiveness and rendering fidelity.
AI.method: SpiD builds a single-image Gaussian head avatar framework with two disentanglement axes: (1) the compute axis internalizes per-frame driving to remove external tracking dependency at inference, and (2) the feature axis splits the avatar into three specialized Gaussian branches, each modeling a geometrically distinct facial domain.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show consistently strong performance against state-of-the-art methods while achieving the fastest inference speed among all compared methods on a single GPU, with the complete driving pipeline included.
AI.conclusion: SpiD demonstrates that disentangling both compute (driving) and feature (facial regions) enables efficient and expressive single-image head avatar synthesis without external tracking dependencies.

title: TongueReenact: Geometry-Anchored Tongue Synthesis for Face Reenactment
summary: Modern face reenactment systems achieve impressive pose and expression transfer using geometry-driven representations. However, they largely ignore tongue dynamics, leading to anatomically inconsistent mouth interiors during speech and expressive motions. We introduce the first framework for cross-identity tongue dynamics transfer in face reenactment. We propose a foundation-model-assisted bootstrapping pipeline that produces a dedicated tongue segmentation model for in-the-wild reenactment without curated annotations. We further introduce a spatially constrained latent masked diffusion model for realistic tongue synthesis, with adaptive mask dilation for seamless mouth boundary transitions. Extensive experiments demonstrate improvements of more than two times over all baselines on every tongue-specific metric. We additionally propose a VLM-based evaluation protocol that replicates expert annotation at scale, confirming perceptual superiority across all ablation variants.

AI.tldr: A framework for cross-identity tongue dynamics transfer in face reenactment, using a foundation-model-assisted bootstrapping pipeline for tongue segmentation and a spatially constrained latent masked diffusion model for realistic tongue synthesis.
AI.motivation: Existing face reenactment systems achieve pose and expression transfer but ignore tongue dynamics, resulting in anatomically inconsistent mouth interiors during speech and expressive motions.
AI.method: The paper proposes: (1) a foundation-model-assisted bootstrapping pipeline to produce a dedicated tongue segmentation model without curated annotations, and (2) a spatially constrained latent masked diffusion model for realistic tongue synthesis with adaptive mask dilation for seamless mouth boundary transitions.
AI.result: Improvements of more than two times over all baselines on every tongue-specific metric. A VLM-based evaluation protocol replicates expert annotation at scale, confirming perceptual superiority across all ablation variants.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework is the first to enable cross-identity tongue dynamics transfer in face reenactment, achieving anatomically consistent mouth interiors with state-of-the-art performance.

title: Temporal Concentration from Rollout Errors: Implicit Preference Optimization for Text-to-Video Diffusion
summary: Recent advances in preference alignment for diffusion-based video generation, particularly via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), have significantly improved visual quality. However, temporally sparse artifacts such as motion collapse, object flickering, and color oversaturation remain a major barrier to perceptual realism. Existing methods struggle with these issues due to two key limitations: (1) the preference attribution bottleneck, where offline human annotations are costly and fail to accurately capture learning dynamics, while online reward signals are rollout-aware but often unstable and biased; and (2) temporal credit misallocation, where uniformly applied supervision cannot effectively target the brief segments in which artifacts occur. To address these challenges, we propose concentrated Implicit Preference Optimization (cIPO), a post-training framework for video diffusion models. cIPO derives implicit preference signals directly from the denoising process: given a real video, the model adds forward noise and reconstructs it via iterative denoising, treating the original as the preferred sample and the reconstruction as the dispreferred one. This formulation captures inference-time errors without requiring human annotations or external reward models. Moreover, frame-level discrepancies between original and reconstructed videos reveal when failures occur. cIPO leverages this by computing temporal reconstruction errors and concentrating optimization on high-error segments, enabling more precise correction of failure-prone regions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that cIPO consistently enhances video authenticity and temporal coherence across multiple datasets, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of implicit preference with temporally concentrated optimization.

AI.tldr: cIPO is a post-training framework for video diffusion models that derives implicit preference signals directly from the denoising process (original video vs. reconstruction) and concentrates optimization on temporally sparse artifact segments using reconstruction errors, improving video authenticity and temporal coherence without human annotations or reward models.
AI.motivation: Existing preference alignment methods (e.g., DPO) struggle with temporally sparse artifacts like motion collapse and flickering due to (1) preference attribution bottleneck—offline human annotations are costly and inaccurate, while online rewards are unstable—and (2) temporal credit misallocation—uniform supervision cannot target brief artifact segments.
AI.method: cIPO adds forward noise to real videos and reconstructs them via iterative denoising, treating the original as preferred and the reconstruction as dispreferred to derive implicit preference signals. It computes frame-level temporal reconstruction errors to identify and concentrate optimization on high-error segments where failures occur.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show cIPO consistently enhances video authenticity and temporal coherence across multiple datasets, demonstrating effectiveness and efficiency of implicit preference with temporally concentrated optimization.
AI.conclusion: Implicit preference derived from the denoising process, combined with temporal concentration on artifact-prone segments, offers a more effective and efficient alternative to existing preference alignment methods for improving perceptual realism in video diffusion models.

title: Landmark shape spaces with induced metrics
summary: We present a unification of Kendall's landmark shape spaces, where rigid motions are factored out and scale fixed on landmark configurations equipped with Euclidean geometry, with landmark configuration spaces carrying Riemannian metrics descending from right-invariant Sobolev metrics on the diffeomorphism group. The resulting new landmark shape spaces achieve the defining properties of both approaches: The regularity of the descending metric prevents landmarks from colliding, the metric is defined in the ambient space independent of the number of landmarks, local rigid transformations are preserved, global rigid motions are removed, and scale fixed. To achieve this, we define a particular Sobolev-type operator, the screened elasticity operator, whose null-space consists exactly of the rigid motions, we show how this operator descends to achieve the desired geometry, and we present approaches to solving matching problems and computing geodesics numerically. The resulting construction allows the use of landmark configuration spaces with sufficiently regular metrics in applications while retaining the shape invariances that are a hallmark of Kendall's shape spaces.

AI.tldr: The paper unifies Kendall's landmark shape spaces (which factor out rigid motions and fix scale) with landmark configuration spaces equipped with Riemannian metrics from right-invariant Sobolev metrics on the diffeomorphism group. A new "screened elasticity operator" with null-space exactly equal to rigid motions enables a metric that prevents landmark collisions, is independent of landmark count, preserves local rigid transformations, removes global rigid motions, and fixes scale.
AI.motivation: Kendall's shape spaces and diffeomorphism-based landmark shape spaces each have desirable but complementary properties. Kendall's spaces provide shape invariances (removing rigid motions and scale) but lack collision prevention and metric regularity. Sobolev metric-based approaches prevent collisions and are independent of landmark count but do not retain the full shape invariance structure. The paper aims to combine both sets of properties.
AI.method: The authors define a specific Sobolev-type operator called the "screened elasticity operator" whose null-space consists exactly of the rigid motions. They show how this operator descends to landmark configuration spaces to produce the desired geometry, and present numerical approaches for solving matching problems and computing geodesics.
AI.result: The resulting landmark shape spaces simultaneously achieve: regularity of the descending metric that prevents landmark collisions, metric definition in the ambient space independent of the number of landmarks, preservation of local rigid transformations, removal of global rigid motions, and fixed scale.
AI.conclusion: The construction enables the use of landmark configuration spaces with sufficiently regular metrics in practical applications while retaining the shape invariances characteristic of Kendall's shape spaces, thus bridging the two previously separate approaches.

title: BladeYOLO: Wind Turbine Blade Defect Detection with Limited Annotations and Weak-Saliency Awareness
comment: Accepted to IEEE TGRS, Code: https://github.com/zhangfangtao/BladeYOLO
summary: Wind turbine blade defect detection remains highly challenging in real-world inspection scenarios due to limited on-site data and the subtle visual characteristics of defects. In practice, blade defects are often small-scale, low-contrast, and difficult to distinguish from complex backgrounds, which significantly limits the robustness of existing detectors. To address these challenges, we propose BladeYOLO, a defect detection framework for wind turbine blades. Specifically, we integrate a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone initialized with DINOv3 self-supervised pre-trained weights into YOLOv12-L, enabling the transfer of large-scale generic visual priors to blade defect detection and improving feature representation under limited training annotations. To enhance the perception of subtle defects, we further develop a Mamba-guided Weak-Defect Enhancement module, which consists of a Detail-Enhanced Multi-scale Branch for preserving high-frequency structural cues and a Cross-Mamba module for progressively propagating high-level semantic guidance to shallow features. In addition, we introduce a lightweight Style-Injector module that captures environment-related style information via Fourier decomposition and injects it into selected ViT self-attention layers, thereby improving robustness against environment-induced appearance variations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BladeYOLO achieves superior performance on the WTBlade-Defect dataset, with additional annotation-budget experiments showing its favorable performance under reduced training annotations. Evaluation on the public Wind Surface Defect dataset further provides supportive evidence for the cross-dataset robustness of BladeYOLO. In particular, on this public dataset, BladeYOLO outperforms the best competing method by 3.5\% in mAP$_{50}$ and 2.5\% in mAP$_{50-95}$.

AI.tldr: BladeYOLO is a wind turbine blade defect detection framework that integrates a ViT backbone with DINOv3 self-supervised pre-training into YOLOv12-L, adds a Mamba-guided Weak-Defect Enhancement module for subtle defect perception, and introduces a Style-Injector for environmental robustness. It achieves superior performance on the WTBlade-Defect dataset and outperforms competitors by 3.5% mAP50 / 2.5% mAP50-95 on the public Wind Surface Defect dataset.
AI.motivation: Blade defect detection is difficult in real-world scenarios due to limited on-site data and subtle visual characteristics (small-scale, low-contrast defects hard to distinguish from complex backgrounds), which limits the robustness of existing detectors.
AI.method: BladeYOLO integrates: (1) a ViT backbone with DINOv3 self-supervised pre-trained weights into YOLOv12-L for transferring large-scale visual priors under limited annotations; (2) a Mamba-guided Weak-Defect Enhancement module with a Detail-Enhanced Multi-scale Branch for high-frequency structural cues and a Cross-Mamba module for propagating high-level semantic guidance to shallow features; (3) a lightweight Style-Injector that captures environment-related style information via Fourier decomposition and injects it into ViT self-attention layers for robustness against appearance variations.
AI.result: BladeYOLO achieves superior performance on the WTBlade-Defect dataset, demonstrates favorable performance under reduced training annotations, and on the public Wind Surface Defect dataset outperforms the best competing method by 3.5% in mAP50 and 2.5% in mAP50-95.
AI.conclusion: BladeYOLO provides an effective solution for wind turbine blade defect detection under limited data and subtle defect conditions, with strong cross-dataset robustness and competitive annotation efficiency.

title: mmRadarTwin: A Measurement-Calibrated Signal-Level Digital Twin Platform for Indoor mmWave Radar
summary: Indoor mmWave radar perception is difficult to reproduce because measured range-angle responses depend on scene geometry, material response, multipath, hardware conventions, and signal processing. Existing ray-tracing and digital-twin tools often expose rendering, channel, or path-level quantities, while radar sensing requires complex signal products that can be processed and compared in the same domain as real FMCW measurements. We present mmRadarTwin, a signal-level and path-attributed digital-twin platform for indoor mmWave radar. mmRadarTwin links a real radar measurement branch with an Unreal Engine scene-simulation branch through a shared receive-channel and range-angle processing interface. The simulator writes complex multi-channel receive grids and exports per-path contribution records that identify the actor, material tag, propagation event, and output-bin support of each simulated return. We evaluate mmRadarTwin in an office deployment using a commodity monostatic mmWave radar and mobile scene-capture hardware. Across 154 measured poses spanning 22 radar locations, the current physics-only path-basis simulator recalls 70.8% of measurement-active geometry-supported response regions in the central usable field of view while exposing residuals caused by weak or missing path support, shifted responses, unsupported anchors, and missing physical mechanisms. Rather than claiming complete radar-map reconstruction or cross-room generalization, mmRadarTwin establishes a practical systems workflow for constructing, comparing, and diagnosing indoor radar digital twins.

AI.tldr: mmRadarTwin is a signal-level, path-attributed digital-twin platform for indoor mmWave radar that bridges real FMCW measurements with Unreal Engine scene simulation through shared receive-channel and range-angle processing, enabling reproducible comparison and diagnosis of radar perception.
AI.motivation: Indoor mmWave radar perception is difficult to reproduce because measured range-angle responses depend on many factors (scene geometry, material response, multipath, hardware, signal processing). Existing ray-tracing and digital-twin tools expose rendering/channel/path-level quantities rather than the complex signal products needed for direct comparison with real FMCW measurements.
AI.method: mmRadarTwin links a real radar measurement branch with an Unreal Engine scene-simulation branch through a shared receive-channel and range-angle processing interface. The simulator generates complex multi-channel receive grids and exports per-path contribution records identifying actor, material tag, propagation event, and output-bin support for each simulated return. Evaluation uses commodity monostatic mmWave radar and mobile scene-capture hardware in an office setting.
AI.result: Across 154 measured poses spanning 22 radar locations, the physics-only path-basis simulator recalls 70.8% of measurement-active geometry-supported response regions in the central usable field of view. Residuals are attributed to weak/missing path support, shifted responses, unsupported anchors, and missing physical mechanisms.
AI.conclusion: Rather than claiming complete radar-map reconstruction or cross-room generalization, mmRadarTwin provides a practical systems workflow for constructing, comparing, and diagnosing indoor radar digital twins, enabling reproducible and attributable analysis.

title: Towards Practical Algorithm Selection for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Medical Imaging
summary: Numerous unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) algori-thms exist, but for clinical practice, selecting the best-suited one along with proper hyperparameters often remains unclear, as the unlabeled deployment (target) domain prevents direct evaluation. We propose a label-free criterion that jointly selects the algorithm and hyperparameters for UDA. Given a pool of candidate models from multiple algorithms trained with different hyperparameters, our approach scores each candidate against an agreement reference, and selects the one with the highest score. The agreement reference is constructed in two levels without using target labels. First, we leverage multiple label-free selection signals, using each to nominate a model within every algorithm. Second, the nominated models are aggregated across algorithms to form a reference prediction for each unlabeled target sample. The candidate whose predictions agree most with this reference is then selected for deployment. Experimental results on four brain MRI and four chest X-ray datasets across seven clinically relevant transfer scenarios show that our method achieves better selection performance than other methods and remains effective across different algorithm pools. Our approach takes a step towards practical, label-free algorithm selection for clinical deployment of UDA.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a label-free criterion for jointly selecting the best UDA algorithm and hyperparameters in clinical settings. The method builds a two-level agreement reference from multiple candidate models and selects the one whose predictions most agree with this reference, showing superior selection performance on brain MRI and chest X-ray datasets across seven clinical transfer scenarios.
AI.motivation: In clinical practice, selecting the best UDA algorithm and hyperparameters is challenging because the unlabeled target domain prevents direct evaluation. This makes it unclear which algorithm to deploy when no target labels are available.
AI.method: The approach constructs a two-level agreement reference without target labels: (1) multiple label-free selection signals nominate a model within each algorithm, and (2) nominated models are aggregated across algorithms to form reference predictions for each unlabeled target sample. The candidate with the highest agreement to this reference is selected for deployment.
AI.result: Experiments on four brain MRI and four chest X-ray datasets across seven clinically relevant transfer scenarios demonstrate better selection performance than other methods, and the approach remains effective across different algorithm pools.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a practical, label-free algorithm selection framework for clinical deployment of UDA, advancing the feasibility of deploying UDA models in real clinical settings without target labels.

title: Face and Voice Cross-modal Association with Learning Convex Feature Embedding
summary: Face-and-voice association learning is one of the most challenging tasks in deep learning. In this paper, we propose a simple but powerful cross-modal feature embedding method for the association of faces and voices. Previous work has studied cross-modal association tasks to establish the correlation between voice clips and facial images. These works have addressed cross-modal discrimination but underestimate the importance of handling heterogeneity in inter-modal features between audio and video, resulting in a lot of false positives and false negatives. To tackle the problem, the proposed method learns the embeddings of cross-modal features by making another feature exist between cross-modal features, facilitating the voice and face features of the same person to be embedded in a convex hull. Moreover, the incorporation of cross-modal attention mechanisms with convex embedding techniques represents a highly effective strategy for the attenuation of false positives and false negatives, accomplished via the minimization of inter-class discrepancies. We exhaustively evaluated our method for cross-modal verification, matching, and retrieval tasks on the large-scale VoxCeleb dataset. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves notable improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a cross-modal feature embedding method for face-and-voice association that uses convex hull embeddings with cross-modal attention mechanisms to reduce false positives and false negatives caused by inter-modal heterogeneity.
AI.motivation: Previous cross-modal face-voice association works address discrimination but underestimate inter-modal feature heterogeneity between audio and video, leading to many false positives and false negatives.
AI.method: The method learns cross-modal feature embeddings by inserting another feature between cross-modal features, embedding face and voice features of the same person within a convex hull. It combines cross-modal attention mechanisms with convex embedding techniques to minimize inter-class discrepancies.
AI.result: Extensive evaluation on cross-modal verification, matching, and retrieval tasks using the large-scale VoxCeleb dataset shows notable improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed convex-embedding-based cross-modal approach effectively handles inter-modal heterogeneity, significantly reducing false positives/negatives and outperforming prior methods on VoxCeleb benchmarks.

title: Collaborative Feature Aggregation for Face Super-Resolution and Robust Re-Identification
summary: We propose a novel collaborative approach for face super-resolution (SR) and robust person re-identification from sequential or multi-view facial images. Traditional SR methods often suffer from blurring and distortion in faces recovered from poor-quality images due to low resolution. Image- and video-based facial SR methods using facial landmarks or segmentation also have similar challenges. To overcome these limitations, we leverage multiple correlated facial observations, across time or viewpoints, by introducing a transformer-based collaborative feature aggregation method that unifies identity features from multi-sequence or multi-view data. This allows faces in multiple sequences of an individual to contribute to accurately estimating common facial features. Furthermore, we propose a cascade SR network to progressively restore the high-resolution image of the target's face with gradual facial feature unification. The unified identity representation is further utilized in person re-identification scenarios, enabling accurate matching even under severe image degradation. The exhaustive experimental results and comparisons show that our method outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating consistent improvements in both face super-resolution and re-identification performance. Our work highlights the effectiveness of joint identity reconstruction and progressive image restoration from multiple facial inputs in enhancing downstream visual recognition tasks.

AI.tldr: A transformer-based collaborative face super-resolution method that aggregates identity features from multiple sequences/views, coupled with a cascade SR network for progressive restoration, and applies the unified identity representation to robust person re-identification under severe image degradation.
AI.motivation: Traditional face super-resolution methods suffer from blurring and distortion due to low resolution, and existing image/video-based facial SR approaches using landmarks or segmentation face similar challenges. The authors aim to overcome these limitations by leveraging multiple correlated facial observations across time or viewpoints.
AI.method: Introduces a transformer-based collaborative feature aggregation method that unifies identity features from multi-sequence or multi-view data, allowing multiple face sequences of an individual to contribute to estimating common facial features. Additionally, proposes a cascade SR network that progressively restores the high-resolution target face while gradually unifying facial features. The unified identity representation is then used for person re-identification.
AI.result: Exhaustive experiments show the method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both face super-resolution and person re-identification, with consistent improvements under severe image degradation.
AI.conclusion: Joint identity reconstruction and progressive image restoration from multiple facial inputs is effective in enhancing downstream visual recognition tasks like person re-identification.

title: Convolutional Neural Shading for High-Quality 3D Reconstruction from Multi-View Images
summary: We propose a convolutional neural shading (CNS), a novel pipeline to reconstruct high-quality 3D shapes from multi-view images. Several recent studies have used neural radiance fields and other neural differentiable rendering methods to understand 3D geometry. However, these approaches rely on single-point geometric information, such as positions and normals of the surface, leading to a lack of detailed local geometry. Our approach addresses the inherent limitations of single-point information by leveraging a neural shader to capture variations even in dark and textureless regions with a convolutional neural shader, resulting in far more accurate geometry predictions. Additionally, our method mitigates surface irregularities at image boundaries by introducing a fine-detail displacement network, which utilizes spatial information of surface geometry and learns fine displacement details by correlating neighboring values in the rendering coordinates. Through extensive experiments, our proposed method has demonstrated significant quality improvements in the reconstructed shapes and rendered images over current state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Convolutional Neural Shading (CNS), a novel 3D reconstruction pipeline that uses a convolutional neural shader to capture local geometric variations and a fine-detail displacement network to mitigate surface irregularities at image boundaries, achieving higher-quality 3D shape reconstruction from multi-view images than current state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Existing neural differentiable rendering methods (e.g., NeRF-based approaches) rely on single-point geometric information like positions and normals on surfaces, which leads to a lack of detailed local geometry. This is particularly problematic in dark and textureless regions where reliable geometric cues are limited.
AI.method: The method introduces two key components: (1) a convolutional neural shader that captures local geometry variations beyond single-point information, effectively handling dark and textureless regions; and (2) a fine-detail displacement network that leverages spatial information of surface geometry and correlates neighboring values in rendering coordinates to reduce surface irregularities at image boundaries.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate significant quality improvements in both reconstructed 3D shapes and rendered images compared to current state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Convolutional neural shading effectively overcomes the limitations of single-point geometric information in neural differentiable rendering, enabling more accurate and detailed 3D shape reconstruction.

title: What Makes Deep Learning Work for Traditional Chinese Medicine Tongue Diagnosis? A Comprehensive Ablation Study
summary: Deep learning has shown promise for automated tongue diagnosis in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), yet the design space remains underexplored. We conducted a systematic ablation study spanning 20+ model versions under rigorous 5-fold cross-validation on TongueDx2 (5,109 images, 976 expert-annotated) and a merged dataset of 11,101 samples. We compared six backbone architectures, four loss functions, five augmentation strategies, and six training strategies. The best 976-sample model achieved weighted-F1 of 0.6625 using ConvNeXt-Tiny with restrained augmentation and weak-group ensemble, while the best 11,101-sample model reached weighted-F1 of 0.7761. Six key design principles emerged: (1) ConvNeXt-Tiny offers optimal parameter efficiency; (2) BCE substantially outperforms Asymmetric Loss (+2.7%); (3) restrained color augmentation is critical; (4) weak-group ensemble replacement (+2.1%) outperforms probability averaging; (5) data scaling yielded +20.6% improvement; (6) expanding from 13 to 45 label dimensions caused catastrophic collapse (0.78 to 0.22). These principles are generalizable to multi-label medical image classification with class imbalance.

AI.tldr: A systematic ablation study of deep learning models for automated tongue diagnosis in TCM, evaluating 20+ model versions across architectures, losses, augmentations, and training strategies on two datasets (5,109 and 11,101 images), yielding six key design principles including ConvNeXt-Tiny as the optimal backbone, BCE loss superiority, and catastrophic collapse when expanding label dimensions.
AI.motivation: Deep learning shows promise for automated tongue diagnosis in traditional Chinese medicine, but the design space for such models remains underexplored. This paper aims to systematically investigate design choices to guide model development.
AI.method: Conducted rigorous 5-fold cross-validation ablation studies spanning 20+ model versions on TongueDx2 (5,109 images, 976 expert-annotated) and a merged dataset of 11,101 samples. Compared six backbone architectures, four loss functions, five augmentation strategies, and six training strategies.
AI.result: Best 976-sample model achieved weighted-F1 of 0.6625 using ConvNeXt-Tiny with restrained augmentation and weak-group ensemble; best 11,101-sample model reached 0.7761. BCE outperformed Asymmetric Loss by +2.7%, weak-group ensemble improved +2.1%, data scaling yielded +20.6%, and expanding from 13 to 45 labels caused collapse from 0.78 to 0.22.
AI.conclusion: Six key design principles emerged that are generalizable to multi-label medical image classification with class imbalance, providing practical guidance for model architecture selection, loss function choice, augmentation strategy, ensemble methods, data scaling, and label dimension management.

title: OPLD: On-Policy Latent Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
summary: Interleaved multimodal Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves visual reasoning by incorporating auxiliary visual evidence into intermediate reasoning. However, existing approaches remain constrained by externally defined reasoning traces and visual operations, limiting their ability to develop flexible and abstract visual thinking. Reasoning with latent has recently offered a promising direction by internalizing intermediate computation into continuous representations. Nevertheless, existing visual-latent methods mainly supervise latent states through alignment with compressed auxiliary visual features, treating them as proxies for visual observations rather than active reasoning states. Consequently, they capture the provided evidence but fail to fully internalize the abstract reasoning process induced by multimodal CoT. In this paper, we propose OPLD (On-Policy Latent Distillation), a simple framework that transfers the reasoning capability induced by privileged multimodal CoT into latent reasoning representations. Extensive experiments on diverse multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that OPLD consistently outperforms existing latent reasoning methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks. The results suggest that supervising latent representations at the reasoning-process level provides a more effective paradigm for multimodal latent reasoning than conventional feature-level alignment.

AI.tldr: OPLD (On-Policy Latent Distillation) is a framework that transfers reasoning capabilities from privileged multimodal Chain-of-Thought into latent reasoning representations, outperforming existing latent reasoning methods on multimodal benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing interleaved multimodal CoT methods rely on externally defined reasoning traces and visual operations, limiting flexible abstract visual thinking. Current visual-latent methods supervise latent states via alignment with compressed auxiliary visual features, which merely captures provided evidence rather than internalizing the abstract reasoning process induced by multimodal CoT.
AI.method: OPLD uses on-policy latent distillation to transfer reasoning capability from privileged multimodal CoT into continuous latent reasoning representations, supervising latent states at the reasoning-process level rather than through conventional feature-level alignment.
AI.result: OPLD consistently outperforms existing latent reasoning methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple diverse multimodal benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Supervising latent representations at the reasoning-process level provides a more effective paradigm for multimodal latent reasoning than conventional feature-level alignment.

title: S-Avatar: Diffusion-Guided Gaussian Head Avatars from a Single Image
summary: We propose S-Avatar, a novel method for generating photorealistic 3D head avatars from a single image using a diffusion-guided 3D model generation module and strategies for animating 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). While single-image head avatar reconstruction is crucial for lifelike Virtual Reality (VR) applications, existing approaches often struggle to preserve 3D consistency under unseen viewpoints. S-Avatar addresses this limitation through a three-stage pipeline. First, a high-resolution 3DGS is synthesized directly from a single image using a diffusion-based Gaussian splat generation module. Next, the parametric head model FLAME is aligned with the generated 3DGS by optimizing its parameters and spatial transformations. Finally, to adapt the 3DGS to FLAME variations, we construct a binding template that encodes the spatial relationship between the initial splats and FLAME. The dynamic 3D head avatar can then be rendered in real time by deforming the 3DGS with the binding template. By combining diffusion-guided canonical 3DGS generation with FLAME-based control, our method achieves efficient and accurate reconstruction with enhanced 3D consistency. Evaluations on public datasets demonstrate that S-Avatar outperforms state-of-the-art methods in novel-view and expression generation, achieving superior realism and consistency. Consequently, our approach represents a significant advance in accessible avatar creation, applicable to a wide range of VR/AR applications. The project page is available at https://github.com/hailsong/savatar.

AI.tldr: S-Avatar generates photorealistic 3D head avatars from a single image using a three-stage pipeline: diffusion-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) generation, FLAME parametric model alignment, and binding template-based deformation for real-time animation.
AI.motivation: Single-image head avatar reconstruction is crucial for lifelike VR/AR applications, but existing approaches struggle to preserve 3D consistency under unseen viewpoints.
AI.method: A three-stage pipeline: (1) synthesize high-resolution 3DGS directly from a single image using a diffusion-based Gaussian splat generation module; (2) align the parametric FLAME head model with the generated 3DGS by optimizing parameters and spatial transformations; (3) construct a binding template encoding spatial relationships between initial splats and FLAME, enabling dynamic deformation of 3DGS for real-time rendering.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in novel-view and expression generation on public datasets, achieving superior realism and consistency.
AI.conclusion: S-Avatar represents a significant advance in accessible avatar creation by combining diffusion-guided canonical 3DGS generation with FLAME-based control, applicable to a wide range of VR/AR applications.

title: Think with Extra-Image: A Farmland Segmentation Agent Driven by Spatio-Temporal Information Gain
summary: Existing farmland remote sensing image (FRSI) segmentation follows a "Think with Intra-Image" paradigm, assuming that the current image contains sufficient visual evidence for reliable segmentation. Yet farmland appearance varies with phenology and spatial context and is often confused with other land-cover, making instantaneous, local observations inadequate. Thus, segmentation ambiguity stems not only from limited model representation, but more fundamentally from the required spatio-temporal information lying beyond the current image. Based on this insight, we redefine FRSI segmentation from an information bottleneck perspective as a dynamic decision process driven by task-relevant extra spatio-temporal information gain. We further propose FarmSeeker, a dynamic FRSI segmentation agent that identifies ambiguous regions, reasons about their causes, and queries extra spatio-temporal information on demand for accurate segmentation. To evaluate FarmSeeker, we construct GSFS-Bench, the first global-scale, high-resolution FRSI segmentation benchmark that supports reasoning-querying. Experiments show that FarmSeeker achieves more stable segmentation performance than existing methods. The project is publicly available at: https://withoutocean.github.io/FarmSeeker/

AI.tldr: FarmSeeker redefines farmland remote sensing image segmentation as a dynamic decision process that queries extra spatio-temporal information on demand for ambiguous regions, supported by GSFS-Bench, the first global-scale benchmark for reasoning-based segmentation.
AI.motivation: Existing FRSI segmentation relies on intra-image information alone, but farmland appearance varies with phenology and spatial context, causing ambiguity that cannot be resolved from a single image. The spatio-temporal information needed for reliable segmentation often lies beyond the current image.
AI.method: FarmSeeker is a dynamic segmentation agent that identifies ambiguous regions, reasons about the causes of ambiguity, and queries extra spatio-temporal information on demand from an information bottleneck perspective. A new benchmark, GSFS-Bench, was constructed to support reasoning-querying evaluation.
AI.result: FarmSeeker achieves more stable segmentation performance than existing methods on the GSFS-Bench benchmark.
AI.conclusion: FRSI segmentation should be reframed as a dynamic decision process incorporating task-relevant extra spatio-temporal information gain, rather than relying solely on intra-image evidence.

title: Scaling Vision-Language Models Is Not Enough to Mitigate Bias
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as CLIP are now foundational to multimodal systems, yet their robustness to spurious correlations remains poorly understood at scale. We present the first large-scale empirical study of 194 publicly available VLMs, including 16 model families, covering a wide range of model sizes, 24 training datasets, and three evaluation benchmarks, namely ImageNet (overall performance), CelebA (typical single-attribute bias), and UrbanCars (complex multi-attribute biases). Across these settings, the Spearman correlation between model scale and performance weakens as evaluation shifts from ImageNet ($ρ{=}0.68$) to single-attribute ($ρ{=}0.48$) and further to multi-attribute ($ρ{=}0.05$) bias benchmarks. In contrast, properties of the training data (size and quality) show more consistent relationships with worst-group accuracy across both bias benchmarks. Notably, curated datasets yield improvements of up to 25% over uncurated alternatives at a comparable scale. Finally, the effect of architectural choices (e.g., patch size, image resolution) is highly context-dependent, varying with the nature of the benchmark, including the type of bias and its spatial distribution within images.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first large-scale empirical study of 194 publicly available VLMs across 16 model families, finding that model scale does not reliably predict robustness to spurious correlations, while training data properties (size and quality) show more consistent relationships with worst-group accuracy.
AI.motivation: While VLMs like CLIP are foundational to multimodal systems, their robustness to spurious correlations at scale remains poorly understood.
AI.method: They conduct a large-scale empirical study of 194 publicly available VLMs covering 16 model families, 24 training datasets, and three evaluation benchmarks: ImageNet (overall performance), CelebA (single-attribute bias), and UrbanCars (multi-attribute biases). They analyze Spearman correlations between model scale, training data properties, and architectural choices against performance on these benchmarks.
AI.result: Scale-based correlations weaken from ImageNet (ρ=0.68) to single-attribute (ρ=0.48) to multi-attribute (ρ=0.05) bias benchmarks. Training data properties show more consistent relationships with worst-group accuracy. Curated datasets yield up to 25% improvements over uncurated alternatives at comparable scale. Architectural effects are highly context-dependent.
AI.conclusion: Model scale is a weak predictor of robustness to spurious correlations, especially for complex multi-attribute biases. Training data quality and curation matter more than scale for bias robustness, while architectural effects depend heavily on evaluation context.

title: FaithEyes: Towards Faithful Tool Use via Multi-Agent Process-Image Verification
summary: Agentic vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave textual reasoning with explicit tool calls such as cropping and code-based image manipulation, have emerged as a compelling paradigm for reliable and interpretable multimodal reasoning. However, recent studies have revealed that such models often use tools unfaithfully. Many process images are irrelevant to the question (e.g., the tool crops the wrong region or misses the queried target), yet the call still receives full credit and the model still answers correctly. Such decorative or misaligned tool calls waste computation and reveal that the model leans on prior knowledge or the original image rather than the evidence it retrieves. This may stem from two limitations of prevailing methods: the tool reward fails to distinguish useful from useless calls, and tool feedback carries no signal of usefulness. To this end, we introduce FaithEyes, a multi-agent self-judging framework. Concretely, we use a VLM to judge whether each process image helps answer the question. The judgement is injected into the reasoning context as part of the tool observation to help subsequent reasoning, and meanwhile is used to scale the tool reward by the helpful-tool ratio to suppress reward hacking. To keep judgement available at evaluation and thus ensure train-test consistency, we further design a multi-agent framework where the model itself serves as a subagent to judge the tool calls from main agent, eliminating any dependence on an external model at inference. Training via a two-stage SFT + RL pipeline on adapted open-source data, FaithEyes attains competitive or superior accuracy across visual perception and reasoning benchmarks, while markedly improving tool faithfulness. The homepage is at https://github.com/Mosi-AI/FaithEyes.

AI.tldr: FaithEyes is a multi-agent self-judging framework that improves tool faithfulness in agentic vision-language models by having a VLM judge whether each process image is helpful, injecting this judgement into the reasoning context, and using it to scale tool rewards during training to suppress reward hacking.
AI.motivation: Agentic VLMs often use tools unfaithfully—making irrelevant or misaligned tool calls that receive full credit despite not contributing to the answer. This stems from two limitations: tool rewards fail to distinguish useful from useless calls, and tool feedback carries no signal of usefulness.
AI.method: FaithEyes uses a VLM judge to evaluate whether each process image helps answer the question. The judgement is injected into the reasoning context as part of tool observation and used to scale tool rewards by helpful-tool ratio. A multi-agent framework enables the model itself to judge tool calls from a main agent, removing external model dependence at inference. Training uses a two-stage SFT + RL pipeline on adapted open-source data.
AI.result: FaithEyes achieves competitive or superior accuracy across visual perception and reasoning benchmarks while markedly improving tool faithfulness compared to baselines.
AI.conclusion: Self-judging tool calls with explicit helpfulness signals effectively reduces decorative tool usage and reward hacking in agentic VLMs, suggesting that incorporating utility feedback into both training signal and context can yield more faithful multimodal reasoning.

title: EgoGenesis: Egocentric World-Action Modeling with Online Anchored Projective Memory and Action-3D RoPE
summary: Egocentric video offers rich manipulation experience for embodied AI, yet collecting diverse egocentric data across scenes, objects, motions, and embodiments remains costly. We present \method, an egocentric world-action simulator that synthesizes controllable, high-quality manipulation videos to expand scarce real-world training data. \method{} builds on a pretrained video generation prior and introduces two geometry-aware conditioning mechanisms. Online Anchored Projective Memory (OAPM) preserves a first-frame 3D scene anchor while periodically refreshing a recent state during autoregressive generation. Action-3D Rotary Position Embedding (A3D-RoPE) encodes end-effector motion with camera-aware 3D rotary coordinates, injecting action geometry into skeleton-to-video cross-attention for precise control. Together, these components improve visual fidelity, geometric stability, and action alignment in long egocentric rollouts. Moreover, augmenting 400 real trajectories with 400 \method-generated trajectories improves out-of-distribution real-robot success from 77\% to 84\% on single-arm tasks and from 53\% to 70\% on dual-arm tasks, demonstrating that the synthesized data substantially improve downstream WAM generalization.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an egocentric world-action simulator (method name not disclosed) that synthesizes controllable, high-quality manipulation videos to augment scarce real-world training data for embodied AI. It introduces two geometry-aware conditioning mechanisms: Online Anchored Projective Memory (OAPM) for 3D scene anchoring and Action-3D Rotary Position Embedding (A3D-RoPE) for precise action control. Augmenting real trajectories with generated ones improves real-robot success from 77% to 84% (single-arm) and 53% to 70% (dual-arm).
AI.motivation: Collecting diverse egocentric manipulation data across scenes, objects, motions, and embodiments is prohibitively expensive, limiting the training of embodied AI systems that could benefit from rich manipulation experience.
AI.method: The method builds on a pretrained video generation prior and introduces two components: (1) Online Anchored Projective Memory (OAPM) which preserves a first-frame 3D scene anchor while periodically refreshing recent state during autoregressive generation, and (2) Action-3D Rotary Position Embedding (A3D-RoPE) which encodes end-effector motion using camera-aware 3D rotary coordinates, injected into skeleton-to-video cross-attention for precise action control.
AI.result: Augmenting 400 real trajectories with 400 generated trajectories improves out-of-distribution real-robot success from 77% to 84% on single-arm tasks and from 53% to 70% on dual-arm tasks, demonstrating substantial downstream World Action Model (WAM) generalization gains.
AI.conclusion: The synthesized egocentric manipulation videos effectively expand scarce real-world training data and meaningfully improve downstream real-robot generalization, showing the practical value of the world-action simulation approach.

title: Space2Ground 2.0: A Multi-Source Dataset and Framework for Agricultural Monitoring through Fusion of Street-Level and Satellite Imagery
comment: This paper has been accepted for presentation at the 45th EARSeL Symposium, Athens, Greece
summary: Accurate and scalable parcel-level agricultural monitoring remains challenging because satellite Earth Observation alone provides only an overhead perspective of agricultural parcels, while optical observations are further affected by cloud-induced temporal gaps. This paper presents Space2Ground 2.0, a multi-source framework integrating Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 multispectral time series with geo-tagged street-level imagery acquired using vehicle-mounted cameras and shared through the Mapillary platform. A largely automated processing pipeline performs semantic filtering, image quality assessment, viewpoint-based parcel association, and dataset refinement, transforming large volumes of crowdsourced imagery into parcel-linked, analysis-ready data. Applied over Cyprus during the 2022 growing season, the pipeline produced a curated dataset of 46,050 annotated street-level images, selected from an initial collection exceeding 900,000 images and linked with satellite information for 8,581 agricultural parcels. The practical value of the dataset was assessed through parcel-level crop classification experiments using both single- and multi-source observations. The results demonstrate that street-level imagery provides complementary fine-scale visual information that enhances classification when integrated with satellite time series. Overall, Space2Ground 2.0 provides an openly available benchmark dataset and a reproducible methodology for multimodal agricultural monitoring, with potential applications in visual verification, reduced reliance on costly field inspections, and data-driven agricultural policy implementation.

AI.tldr: Space2Ground 2.0 is a multi-source framework integrating Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 multispectral time series, and crowdsourced street-level imagery (from Mapillary) for parcel-level agricultural monitoring. Applied over Cyprus in 2022, the pipeline produced a curated dataset of 46,050 annotated images linked to 8,581 agricultural parcels, and crop classification experiments show street-level imagery complements satellite data.
AI.motivation: Satellite Earth Observation alone provides only an overhead perspective of agricultural parcels, and optical observations are hindered by cloud-induced temporal gaps. There is a need for more accurate and scalable parcel-level agricultural monitoring that can overcome these limitations.
AI.method: A multi-source framework integrating Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 multispectral time series with geo-tagged street-level imagery from the Mapillary platform. A largely automated processing pipeline performs semantic filtering, image quality assessment, viewpoint-based parcel association, and dataset refinement to transform crowdsourced imagery into parcel-linked, analysis-ready data. Parcel-level crop classification experiments were conducted using single- and multi-source observations.
AI.result: The pipeline produced a curated dataset of 46,050 annotated street-level images from an initial collection of over 900,000 images, linked with satellite information for 8,581 agricultural parcels over Cyprus during the 2022 growing season. Street-level imagery provides complementary fine-scale visual information that enhances classification accuracy when integrated with satellite time series.
AI.conclusion: Space2Ground 2.0 provides an openly available benchmark dataset and reproducible methodology for multimodal agricultural monitoring, with potential applications in visual verification, reduced reliance on costly field inspections, and data-driven agricultural policy implementation.

title: TARS: Timestep-Aware Data Scaling for 3D-Free Video Re-Shooting
summary: Video re-shooting aims to regenerate videos with controllable camera motion and viewpoint. Existing methods rely on explicit 3D priors, which are limited by reconstruction quality and often perform poorly when synthesizing previously unseen regions, or on paired videos with different camera trajectories, whose scarcity hinders generalization. We revisit video re-shooting through text-driven semantic viewpoint specification, enabling control over shot scale, viewing angle, and first-/third-person perspective. To this end, we propose TARS, a 3D-free video re-shooting paradigm. Timestep-wise sensitivity analysis reveals that camera motion is primarily established during high-noise stages, where coarse spatiotemporal structures are formed. Based on this insight, we introduce self-supervised training to learn camera dynamics and fundamental visual representations without paired re-shooting data or 3D reconstruction. Through data scaling and joint textual-camera conditioning, TARS supports robust camera and viewpoint control, plausibly synthesizing regions beyond the source view under large camera motions while enabling reverse-angle re-shooting and perspective switching. Extensive experiments show that TARS provides more accurate and temporally consistent camera control than prior methods. Project Page: https://ymlinfeng.github.io/TARS.github.io/

AI.tldr: TARS is a 3D-free video re-shooting paradigm that enables text-driven semantic viewpoint control (shot scale, viewing angle, perspective) through self-supervised training during high-noise diffusion stages, without requiring 3D reconstruction or paired re-shooting data.
AI.motivation: Existing video re-shooting methods either rely on explicit 3D priors that struggle with unseen regions, or paired videos with different camera trajectories that are scarce and hinder generalization. The authors aim to overcome these limitations by revisiting re-shooting as a text-driven semantic viewpoint specification problem.
AI.method: TARS leverages timestep-wise sensitivity analysis revealing that camera motion is established during high-noise denoising stages where coarse spatiotemporal structures form. Based on this, self-supervised training learns camera dynamics without paired data or 3D reconstruction, combined with joint textual-camera conditioning and data scaling.
AI.result: TARS supports robust camera and viewpoint control, plausibly synthesizes regions beyond the source view under large camera motions, enables reverse-angle re-shooting and perspective switching, and provides more accurate and temporally consistent camera control than prior methods.
AI.conclusion: Text-driven semantic viewpoint specification is a viable 3D-free alternative to explicit 3D priors or paired video data for video re-shooting, with self-supervised training on high-noise stages being key to learning camera dynamics.

title: Theia: Large-Scale Multimodal Captioning and Automated Validation of the Incidents1M Dataset for Data-Free Distillation
summary: The deployment of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in critical domains like disaster management requires high-quality multimodal datasets, especially for transferring knowledge via Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (DFKD). However, existing datasets in this domain either entirely lack descriptive text, such as Incidents1M, or suffer from severe text-image semantic misalignment, such as CrisisMMD. In this work, we present a novel methodology to construct and automatically validate a large-scale multimodal dataset for disaster response. Starting from the vision-only Incidents1M, we successfully recovered 100,000 images and generated high-fidelity textual descriptions using two distinct Qwen3.5 architectures: a 4B dense model and a 35B Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model. To ensure the generated captions provide reliable semantic anchoring for DFKD, we introduce an image-blind LLM-as-a-Judge validation pipeline leveraging Qwen3.5-9B. By intentionally obscuring the original image from the judge, this evaluator accurately simulates the modality gap of the student model during data-free distillation. Our evaluation across 173,179 label pairs demonstrates a high semantic agreement (78.65/100) between the two architectures. Furthermore, the automated evaluation reveals a conservative captioning behaviour, characterized by a high Precision (77.6%) and low Recall (46.0%). This minimizes the false positive noise, while simultaneously exposing underlying human annotation inconsistencies in the original ground truth. This work provides a scalable, LLM-validated multimodal dataset and a reproducible framework to advance cross-modal knowledge distillation.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a methodology to construct and automatically validate a large-scale multimodal disaster response dataset. Starting from the vision-only Incidents1M, the authors recover 100,000 images and generate captions using two Qwen3.5 architectures (4B dense and 35B MoE). They introduce an image-blind LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline using Qwen3.5-9B to validate caption quality by simulating the student model's modality gap in DFKD. Evaluation across 173,179 label pairs shows high semantic agreement (78.65/100) between architectures, with conservative captioning (77.6% precision, 46.0% recall) that minimizes false positives while exposing human annotation inconsistencies.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal datasets for disaster management lack descriptive text (e.g., Incidents1M) or suffer from severe text-image semantic misalignment (e.g., CrisisMMD), making them unsuitable for Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (DFKD) where high-quality multimodal data is critical.
AI.method: The authors recover 100,000 images from vision-only Incidents1M and generate textual descriptions using two Qwen3.5 architectures (4B dense and 35B MoE). They introduce an image-blind LLM-as-a-Judge validation pipeline using Qwen3.5-9B that intentionally obscures the original image to simulate the modality gap of the student model during data-free distillation.
AI.result: Evaluation across 173,179 label pairs yields a high semantic agreement (78.65/100) between the two captioning architectures. The automated evaluation shows conservative captioning behavior with 77.6% precision and 46.0% recall, minimizing false positive noise while exposing human annotation inconsistencies in the original ground truth.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a scalable, LLM-validated multimodal dataset and a reproducible framework to advance cross-modal knowledge distillation in disaster response applications.

title: MSCM-net: A hyperspectral image classiffcation method based on multi-scale convolution and Mamba
summary: Hyperspectral imaging is widely used in remote sensing and engineering. Therefore, research on its classification methods is crucial. While CNN and Transformer-based methods have advanced, they still face locality constraints and high computational complexity. To address these issues, we propose an innovative hyperspectral image classification model, MSCM-net. Specifically, first of all, a model architecture combining multi-scale CNN and Mamba is proposed. It consists of a multi-scale feature extraction module (MCSE) and multiple stacked Mamba blocks, which integrates the local feature extraction capability of multi-scale CNN and the long sequence modeling advantage of Mamba. Secondly, the proposed MCSE module consists of multi-scale convolution and SENet. Convolution kernels of different scales extract local information with different receptive fields, enhancing the fusion of spatial and spectral information. Meanwhile, the SENet enables the model to automatically learn the importance of each channel in the multi-scale features. Furthermore, we also propose a dual-branch feature aggregation module, which further effectively extracts and integrates the spectral information contained in the central pixel and the spatial information in the surrounding pixels. Our model has undergone numerous experiments on three widely used benchmark datasets. The experimental results show that MSCM-net can achieve advanced classification performance while reducing computational complexity.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes MSCM-net, a hyperspectral image classification model combining multi-scale CNN and Mamba architecture, featuring a multi-scale feature extraction module (MCSE) with SENet and a dual-branch feature aggregation module, achieving advanced classification performance with reduced computational complexity on three benchmark datasets.
AI.motivation: While CNN and Transformer-based hyperspectral classification methods have advanced, they still suffer from locality constraints and high computational complexity. The authors aim to address these limitations by combining the local feature extraction capabilities of multi-scale CNN with the long sequence modeling advantage of Mamba.
AI.method: The model, MSCM-net, consists of: (1) a multi-scale feature extraction module (MCSE) combining multi-scale convolution kernels with SENet for automatic channel importance learning; (2) stacked Mamba blocks for long sequence modeling; and (3) a dual-branch feature aggregation module that extracts central pixel spectral information and surrounding pixel spatial information separately, then integrates them.
AI.result: Experiments on three widely used benchmark datasets show that MSCM-net achieves advanced classification performance while simultaneously reducing computational complexity compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed MSCM-net effectively addresses the limitations of existing hyperspectral classification methods by integrating multi-scale CNN and Mamba architectures, achieving a favorable balance between classification accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Beyond Visual Ambiguity: Guiding Robust Monocular Depth Estimation in Challenging Scenarios via Detailed Long Captions
summary: Monocular depth estimation (MDE) faces challenges with non-Lambertian surfaces and adverse weather conditions due to the visual ambiguities inherent in single-image limited information. Existing works address them in isolation via image inpainting or augmentation, yielding limited robustness gains.
